About Abridge

Abridge was founded in 2018 with the mission of powering deeper understanding in healthcare. Our AI-powered platform was purpose-built for medical conversations, improving clinical documentation efficiencies while enabling clinicians to focus on what matters most—their patients.

Our enterprise-grade technology transforms patient-clinician conversations into structured clinical notes in real-time, with deep EMR integrations. Powered by Linked Evidence and our purpose-built, auditable AI, we are the only company that maps AI-generated summaries to ground truth, helping providers quickly trust and verify the output. As pioneers in generative AI for healthcare, we are setting the industry standards for the responsible deployment of AI across health systems.

We are a growing team of practicing MDs, AI scientists, PhDs, creatives, technologists, and engineers working together to empower people and make care make more sense. We have offices located in the Mission District in San Francisco, the SoHo neighborhood of New York, and East Liberty in Pittsburgh.

The Role

Abridge is launching a Forward Deployed Engineering motion to go deeper with our health system partners. As one of the founding Forward Deployed Product Managers, you will run focused engagements with our health system partners: going on-site to understand the workflow gap, scoping the engagement with the partner, and owning the outcome end-to-end. You will lead a pod and feed your learnings from the field directly back into the core Abridge product.

This is a role for a senior product leader who can earn the trust of CMOs, CMIOs, CIOs, and operational leaders inside large health systems, while staying close enough to our core product roadmap to make sharp technical trade-offs in real time. You will set the tone for what forward deployed means at Abridge: deep, fast, opinionated, and focused on solving our partners’ most burning problems, which in turn strengthens our core product suite overall.

This role is based out of our San Francisco office and is in-person Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Please only apply if you are open to relocation and our hybrid in-person model in San Francisco.

What You’ll Do

  • Run discovery on-site at our partner accounts. Meet with the executive sponsor, clinicians, and integration teams to scope the engagement and define success before any code is written.

  • Lead a small pod through focused, sprint-style engagements, protecting pod focus and pace.

  • Own the product and feature answer for the engagement, partnering with Partner Success on the broader commercial relationship.

  • Decide what gets built, what gets declined, and what gets routed to the core roadmap. Hold the line on bespoke requests that don't generalize back to the core product.

  • Partner with internal product and engineering teams when an engagement surfaces a net-new product build that belongs on a different track.

What you'll bring

  • 7+ years of product management experience shipping products that users love, with a track record of owning product areas end-to-end.

  • Builder mentality. You've personally driven products from discovery through launch and iteration. You care about craft and quality in what you ship.

  • Strong user empathy and product taste. You instinctively know the difference between a product that works and one that delights.

  • Comfort with ambiguity. You can take a messy problem space and create a clear roadmap without waiting for perfect information.

  • Cross-functional credibility. You can go deep with engineers on technical tradeoffs, partner with design on interaction details, and operate as the senior product
    voice in front of CMOs, CMIOs, CIOs, and CFOs.

  • Track record of running time-bound, outcome-oriented engagements where the deliverable was a live system, not a document.

  • Willingness to travel ~20% on average, with surge periods around engagement kickoff and go-live.

Bonus points if:

  • Healthcare or clinical workflow experience, or familiarity with Epic or other EHR platforms.

  • Prior experience in a forward deployed, solutions engineering, or customer-facing product role at an enterprise AI company.

Why Work at Abridge?

At Abridge, we’re transforming healthcare delivery experiences with generative AI, enabling clinicians and patients to connect in deeper, more meaningful ways. Our mission is clear: to power deeper understanding in healthcare. We’re driving real, lasting change, with millions of medical conversations processed each month.

Joining Abridge means stepping into a fast-paced, high-growth startup where your contributions truly make a difference. Our culture requires extreme ownership—every employee has the ability to (and is expected to) make an impact on our customers and our business.

Beyond individual impact, you will have the opportunity to work alongside a team of curious, high-achieving people in a supportive environment where success is shared, growth is constant, and feedback fuels progress. At Abridge, it’s not just what we do—it’s how we do it. Every decision is rooted in empathy, always prioritizing the needs of clinicians and patients.

We’re committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally. Whether it's flexible work hours, an inclusive culture, or ongoing learning opportunities, we are here to help you thrive and do the best work of your life.

If you are ready to make a meaningful impact alongside passionate people who care deeply about what they do, Abridge is the place for you.

  • Compensation and Equity: Competitive compensation and equity grants for full time employees.

  • ... and much more!

POSITION SUMMARY

FUNDINGO is seeking an Implementation Manager to join our growing Delivery team. You are the primary point of contact for clients during onboarding, responsible for managing the timeline, scope, risks, and communication while configuring the FUNDINGO platform to meet each client's business needs.

You will manage multiple concurrent implementations, run client working sessions independently, and answer most client questions on your own. You will partner with our Solutions Consultant, who owns solution design for complex or unique requirements, advises on edge cases and best practices, and validates the approach when a project reaches the limits of standard functionality.

FUNDINGO is a Salesforce-native loan management platform helping lenders manage the complete lending lifecycle, including origination, servicing, accounting, borrower management, and workflow automation.

Our customers include non-bank lenders, private lenders, CDFIs, financial institutions, and organizations with complex lending operations. FUNDINGO serves as a mission-critical operating platform that powers how these organizations run their businesses.

Our implementations can be complex and highly configurable, requiring coordination across customers, project managers, implementation resources, product experts, engineering, QA, and third-party vendors.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Implementation Ownership

  • Own assigned implementations day to day, leading clients through the full lifecycle from kickoff through training and go-live.

  • Manage project timelines, scope, milestones, and deliverables across multiple concurrent client projects.

  • Identify project risks early, discuss mitigation strategies with the client, and escalate issues when necessary.

  • Prepare daily and/or weekly status reports and communicate regularly with clients, obtaining feedback and approval throughout configuration.

  • Manage the Jira board for assigned projects, ensuring tickets are properly prioritized, assigned, and tracked to meet deadlines.

Client Engagement & Requirements

  • Run requirements and configuration working sessions with clients independently.

  • Ask questions to fully understand client processes from start to finish, applying logical thinking to identify gaps and clarify the underlying need before proposing an approach.

  • Serve as the first line of answers for client questions about FUNDINGO functionality and configuration.

Configuration & Delivery

  • Learn the FUNDINGO platform deeply and configure and test standard product functionality, including pages, fields, flows, and layouts, to meet client business needs.

  • Connect business requirements to specific configuration decisions, considering downstream impacts before making changes.

  • Troubleshoot configuration issues independently before escalating, and document issues clearly for the development team when escalation is needed.

  • Write detailed tickets based on gathered requirements, clearly outlining requirements, acceptance criteria, and relevant details.

  • Guide and assist clients through the data conversion and data migration process.

  • Develop training and configuration documentation to support internal and external stakeholders.

Collaboration with Solutions Consultant

  • Recognize when a requirement is complex, unique, or outside standard product functionality, and bring in the Solutions Consultant for solution design.

  • Execute solution designs provided by the Solutions Consultant and keep them informed of implementation progress and issues.

  • Apply recommended implementation patterns and configuration standards consistently across projects.

Continuous Improvement

  • Share feedback from client implementations to help improve FUNDINGO products, processes, and templates.

  • Record time spent on projects daily to ensure accurate tracking and reporting.

  • Attain quarterly and annual objectives defined collaboratively with management.

  • Additional tasks as assigned.

REQUIREMENTS

  • 3-5 years of relevant experience in product implementation, business analysis, consulting, technical support, or technical problem-solving.

  • Salesforce administration, including building objects, fields, page layouts, and flows

  • Demonstrated ownership of implementation work across multiple phases, from requirements through go-live.

  • Strong communication and customer relations skills, with a consultative approach to understanding client needs.

  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and adapt quickly to changing priorities in a fast-paced environment.

NICE TO HAVES

  • 2+ years of lending experience (loan origination, servicing, CDFI, or alternative lending)

  • Experience in client services in a B2B/SaaS environment

  • Project Lead or Project Management experience

  • Data Migration experience

  • Jira experience

WHAT WE OFFER

The opportunity

  • Be part of the legacy of a growing company at an inflection point, with the chance to make a real impact on our mission

  • Build and operate the delivery engine behind increasingly complex and enterprise-level customer engagements.

  • Take meaningful ownership rather than inheriting a narrowly defined corporate function.

  • Work directly with company leadership and have visibility into the broader business.

  • Build a function that can grow in scope and responsibility as FUNDINGO grows.

  • Help shape the operating model of a Salesforce-native lending technology company.

  • Work in a fully remote environment with a distributed team.

The package

  • Stronger Together
  • Be the Difference
  • Relentless Improvement
These values shape who we are: a dedicated, inventive, and passionate team committed to empowering law firms to achieve lasting growth and success.

The role

You own two growth engines at Centerbase: events and content. Every event you run should create pipeline or deepen a customer relationship. Every piece of content should help Sales win a deal or help Customer Success keep a client.
This is a hands-on role. You set the strategy and you do the work. You run our tradeshows and regional field events alongside Sales. You host our customers. Then you turn those moments into content that keeps working long after the booth comes down.
You report to the CMO. You work side by side with Sales and Customer Success leaders every week. You bring an AI-forward mindset and use it to plan and measure faster than a traditional team could.

• Results. Measure content by pipeline influence and engagement, not output volume.

jobs.description:
About Us:

BukuWarung is SEA’s fastest growing startup and we are building the digital infrastructure for 60 million MSMEs in Indonesia, enabling them to efficiently manage and grow their business, starting with digital bookkeeping, online storefront & payments. BukuWarung’s vision is to empower 60 million MSMEs in Indonesia to become financially aware and enable them to manage and grow their business using technology.

BukuWarung is backed by top tier VCs globally: Peter Thiel’s Valar Ventures, Goodwater Capital, Y-Combinator, AC Ventures, Quona Capital, East Ventures, Golden Gate Ventures, , Tanglin Venture Partners and strategic angel investors from Stripe, PayPal, Plaid, Grab, Gojek, Facebook, AirBnB, Fast, Mastercard etc.


Job Overview

We are looking for a Legal Associate (Litigation) to manage and support legal disputes, investigations, and contentious matters across the business. This role will be responsible for handling a wide range of cases, including fraud, employment disputes, regulatory issues, and other operational legal matters, while ensuring proper coordination with internal stakeholders and external counsel.

The role requires a hands-on legal professional who can analyze risks, manage cases end-to-end, and provide practical legal solutions in a fast-paced environment. You will also support legal documentation, regulatory engagement, and day-to-day legal matters to ensure the company remains compliant and well-protected from legal exposure.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage and support litigation, dispute, and investigation matters across the business, including civil, criminal, regulatory, and administrative cases.

  • Handle dispute-related matters involving merchant fraud, employee fraud, payment-related issues, lending-related issues, and other business operational disputes.

  • Assist in managing employment and industrial relations disputes, including internal investigations, disciplinary matters, employee misconduct cases, settlement discussions, and proceedings before relevant authorities or courts.

  • Respond to and coordinate on police summons, witness interviews, investigations, and other law enforcement-related matters, including preparing supporting documents and liaising with relevant internal teams.

  • Draft, review, and manage legal correspondence relating to disputes and investigations, including warning letters, demand letters, responses to claims, settlement communications, and official submissions to regulators or authorities.

  • Support the legal risk management process by identifying, assessing, and advising on contentious legal issues arising from payment and lending activities, and provide practical recommendations to mitigate potential exposure.

  • Assist in handling incidental legal cases, including competition law matters such as KPPU proceedings, as well as incidental civil, criminal, or regulatory matters that may arise from time to time.

  • Coordinate with and manage external counsel, including monitoring case strategy, timelines, deliverables, and legal spend.

  • Work closely with cross-functional stakeholders, including compliance, risk, fraud, HR, operations, and business teams, to gather facts, develop legal positions, and ensure consistent case handling.

  • Prepare case summaries, legal analyses, evidence, and internal updates for management and key stakeholders.

  • Monitor developments in litigation, dispute resolution, employment, fraud, competition, and financial services laws and regulations relevant to the company’s business.

  • Maintain proper documentation and case records, and ensure timely reporting and escalation of material legal disputes and risks.

  • Provide legal support across the organization based on company-wide priorities, particularly in high-urgency or high-impact situations.

  • Handle day-to-day legal matters including drafting, reviewing, negotiating, and managing various commercial and employment-related agreements such as NDAs, vendor and procurement contracts, consultancy agreements, and other basic non-strategic third-party agreements, as well as employment and industrial relations contracts, including overseeing and supporting the implementation of such agreements.

Requirements & Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Law from a reputable university in Indonesia

  • 5–7 years of solid experience, preferably from Jakarta’s prominent litigation law firms

  • PERADI License is mandatory

  • Additional certifications or other relevant legal certifications are highly preferred

  • Strong exposure to litigation, fraud cases, employment disputes, and regulatory matters

  • Fluent in English, both written and spoken

  • Agile, resilient, and willing to travel as required

  • Strong analytical thinking, sound legal judgment, and excellent communication skills

  • Highly responsible, detail-oriented, able to work independently, and comfortable in a fast-paced environment

  • Male candidate preferred

Mandatory Documents

  • Curriculum Vitae (CV)

  • Diploma Certificate

  • Academic Transcript

  • PERADI License (and other certifications, if available)

The Company

Versaterm is a PE-backed, high-growth SaaS company building a fully integrated platform across the entire public safety ecosystem — dispatch, law enforcement, forensics, courts, and beyond. We've grown through strategic acquisitions and deep product investment. What connects all of it is a single purpose: give public safety agencies the tools and insights to make better decisions in high-stakes moments.

When a 911 call is answered, a detective investigates a case, or a forensic lab processes evidence, there's a good chance our software is working behind the scenes. That's been true for over four decades.

AI is central to where we're going. Not as a feature but as core infrastructure. We're embedding intelligence directly into the workflows our customers rely on every day, and we're doing it alongside them. Our customers tell us what the mission demands. We build what answers it.

This work attracts a specific kind of person — someone who wants to be pushed by great people, build things that outlast a sprint cycle, and go home knowing the work connected back to something real.

The Role

The Senior Demand Generation Manager is responsible for driving sustainable long-term pipeline growth and market engagement across Versaterm’s portfolio of public safety solutions. This role leads high-complexity, cross-departmental initiatives through expertise and influence, and brings deep functional and technical mastery of demand generation. The Senior Demand Generation Manager frequently represents the marketing function in cross-departmental and external engagements, contributes directly to decisions that shape the direction of the area, mentors others, and actively champions Versaterm’s values across the teams and work they influence.

Obtaining and maintaining all required security clearances is a condition of employment. jobs.excerpt: Colure Health builds technology that amplifies the impact of real clinicians.
jobs.description:
Colure Health builds technology that amplifies the impact of real clinicians. Our care platform blends intelligent automation with compassionate workflows, helping physicians stay connected to their patients and deliver better outcomes with less friction. We believe innovation should serve people, and we’re committed to creating tools that empower every provider to improve the health, experience, and quality of life of the communities they serve.

POSITION SUMMARY

The IT Technical Support Specialist keeps Colure Health’s people productive and secure. This role is the first point of contact for technology issues across the executive team, US staff and the international care team in the Philippines, Ecuador and Colombia. It manages devices, accounts and everyday systems, and applies the security controls that protect patient data. As Colure adds clinics and staff, this role will help build repeatable onboarding, offboarding and support processes.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

End-User Support

  • Provide Tier 1 and Tier 2 support by ticket, chat, phone and remote session for hardware, software, accounts, VoIP and connectivity.
  • Troubleshoot issues affecting care coordinators and enrollment staff, including softphones, headsets, CRM and platform access, and home-network problems, often across time zones.
  • Document resolutions and maintain the knowledge base and self-help guides.

Accounts and Access

  • Provision and deprovision user accounts, email, licenses and application access, in coordination with HR and in line with least-privilege principles.
  • Complete same-day access removal at offboarding and support periodic access reviews.
  • Administer password resets, MFA enrollment and single sign-on support.

Devices and Assets

  • Configure, enroll and maintain laptops and mobile devices in mobile device management (MDM), with encryption, screen lock and endpoint protection enforced.
  • Maintain the hardware and software asset inventory, including shipping, retrieval and secure wiping of devices.
  • Apply patches and updates, and track compliance with device security standards.

Systems and Security Support

  • Administer productivity and collaboration tools, such as Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, the phone system and video conferencing.
  • Support the Cybersecurity Specialist with phishing reports, alert triage, and evidence collection for audits.
  • Set up technology for new clinic locations, including workstations, printers, networking and peripherals, with vendor coordination as needed.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 2+ years of IT help desk or desktop support experience.
  • Hands-on experience with Windows and macOS, Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, and an MDM platform such as Intune, Jamf or Kandji.
  • Comfortable supporting remote users, including some international users, by phone, chat and remote-access tools.
  • Understanding of basic networking (DNS, DHCP, Wi-Fi, VPN) and of security practices such as MFA and encryption.
  • Clear, patient communication and strong documentation habits.
  • Ability to work a schedule that covers part of US Eastern Time business hours, with occasional after-hours support.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • CompTIA A+, Network+ or Security+, or Google IT Support certification.
  • Experience in a healthcare or other HIPAA-regulated environment.
  • Experience with ticketing systems such as Jira Service Management, Freshservice or Zendesk.
  • Experience with VoIP and contact-center platforms.
  • Conversational Spanish, to support team members in Ecuador and Colombia.

MEASURES OF SUCCESS

  • Within 90 days: documented onboarding and offboarding checklists and an accurate device inventory.
  • Ongoing: first-response and resolution times within agreed service levels, and same-day access removal for every departing workforce member.

PRIVACY, SECURITY AND CONDUCT

  • Completes HIPAA privacy and security training at hire and annually, and acknowledges Colure’s workforce confidentiality policies.
  • Accesses protected health information (PHI) only to the minimum necessary for assigned duties, using company-issued, managed devices and approved systems.
  • Reports suspected security incidents, privacy concerns or policy violations immediately to the Chief Technology Officer and the Chief People and Privacy Officer.
  • Satisfactory completion of a pre-employment background check, as permitted by applicable law, is a condition of employment.

WORK ENVIRONMENT AND SCHEDULE

Remote work from a private, secure workspace within the United States, with a reliable high-speed internet connection. Scheduled shifts cover part of US Eastern Time business hours and may include occasional evening or weekend coverage. Occasional travel to support clinic setups. As a non-exempt position, all hours worked are recorded and overtime is paid in accordance with applicable law; overtime must be approved in advance.

COMPENSATION

The pay range for this position is $26.00 to $34.00 per hour. Final pay is based on skills, experience and location, and is set within the range. Benefits information will be provided during the interview process.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Colure Health is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status or any other status protected by applicable federal, state or local law. Reasonable accommodations are available to qualified applicants and employees with disabilities upon request.

ROLE MODIFICATION

This description reflects the principal duties of the position and is not an exhaustive list. The scope and role may be modified at any time by the Chief Executive Officer or the Chief Technology Officer when required. jobs.description:
Koyfin is a fast growing fintech company building a powerful, intuitive analytics platform used by financial advisors and individual investors to research ideas, manage portfolios, and grow their businesses. We believe every investor deserves world-class research tools without the complexity or price tag of legacy platforms.

Our impact so far:

🚀 One of the fastest-growing platforms for financial advisors, driven by product-led growth
🥇 Recognized by users as a top-rated investment solution on G2
🏆 Rated as the top research platform for user satisfaction in the Kitces survey, the largest survey in the advisor industry

Reporting to the Head of Sales, this is a from-scratch build. Koyfin has over 60,000 financial advisors using the platform, and over 800,000 registered users. Koyfin is standing up a GTM Engineer function for the first time to help the sales team improve the sales assist motion to the existing registered users. You’ll be working directly with the Head of Sales to build the systems, data, and messaging infrastructure the rest of the org runs on. We are looking for someone to support existing AEs, newly hired SDRs and the Head of Sales to run tests, build reporting and create efficiently run motions to reach aggressive goals.

This is a builder role, not a maintainer role. You'll be defining: a funnel, a lead-scoring model, a reporting layer, an outbound message library that does not yet exist, in a company that runs lean and expects you to own outcomes.

Compensation: The base salary range for this role is $115,000 to $135,000, plus a performance bonus of up to $25,000 per year tied to team pipeline and revenue goals, paid quarterly. The role also includes equity options and medical, dental, and vision coverage for eligible US employees. Final base salary will depend on experience, skills, and location.

What you'll own

CRM, systems & data (foundational)

  • Full ownership of HubSpot: administration, integrations, and data quality

  • Own and expand enrichment and automated workflows for new registrants and existing users (e.g., Clay, HubSpot workflows, API integrations)

  • Define and document the funnel from lead to deal created, including the lead-scoring model

Reporting & analytics

  • Build the dashboards, reporting, and forecasting infrastructure the org uses to judge whether a motion is working

  • Own test-validation tooling for time-boxed motion tests

Outbound messaging

  • Create and iterate all prospect-facing messaging across email and LinkedIn, working in tandem with the SDRs on targeting and sequencing

  • Own message performance (reply rates, positive-reply definition) as an input to the funnel data above

Partnership & process

  • Work alongside AEs and SDRs day to day to identify what’s working, iterate and improve

What we're looking for

  • 5–8+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or GTM analytics

  • Deep, hands-on HubSpot experience (admin-level) or equivalent depth in a comparable CRM; comfortable owning integrations and data architecture, not just reporting on top of them (there is a full engineering team available on an as-needed basis)

  • Hands-on with enrichment and automation tooling (e.g., Clay, Zapier/n8n, APIs/webhooks); SQL or scripting a plus

  • Strong analytical skills with ability to build funnel definitions, lead-scoring models, and forecasting from scratch, without a data team behind you

  • Experience writing and iterating outbound sales copy (email and LinkedIn), or directly overseeing it, since this role owns messaging end to end here, not just the systems around it

  • Comfortable in ambiguity: this is a two-person function (you and the Head of Sales) inside a five-person sales org, and you'll be setting definitions and processes that don't currently exist

  • Fintech, financial data, or advisor-facing SaaS experience a plus, not required

Why Join Koyfin

  • Competitive Compensation: Enjoy a competitive salary, equity options, and a comprehensive benefits package

jobs.description:
About the Role

We are seeking a detail-oriented and knowledgeable Payroll Associate Account Manager to manage and execute accurate, timely payroll services across multiple states. This role serves as the primary point of contact for assigned clients, ensuring payroll operations are compliant with federal, state, and local laws. The ideal candidate will have experience in multi-state payroll processing, tax filings, and payroll compliance, with strong client communication and problem-solving skills.

Day to day, you'll...

  • Serve as the primary payroll contact for a portfolio of assigned clients
  • Process payroll-related actions, including status changes, separations, tax changes, deductions, and direct deposits
  • Apply for and maintain State and Local Withholding IDs; update rates as required by regulation changes
  • Ensure payrolls are processed accurately and on schedule, including regular wages, overtime, bonuses, tips, and other premium payments
  • Review, verify, and reconcile payroll data in accordance with payroll guidelines and compliance requirements
  • Provide clear and timely responses to client inquiries on payroll, policies, and benefits-related topics
  • Manage payroll processes across multiple states and ensure compliance with varying jurisdictional requirements
  • Maintain and update employee payroll records and documentation
  • Support payroll year-end activities, including W-2/1099 issuance and compliance reporting
  • Prepare and file quarterly and annual payroll tax forms; process amended returns when necessary.
  • Distribute federal and state payroll filings to clients and respond to related inquiries
  • Understand and facilitate related payroll services such as workers' compensation reporting and timekeeping systems
  • Interpret and process various earnings and deductions, including garnishments, benefits, and retirement contributions

Required Qualifications

  • 3+ years of experience in payroll processing, preferably in a multi-state environment
  • Bachelors Degree in Accounting or Finance or experience in a similar field
  • Strong working knowledge of federal, state, and local payroll regulations
  • Experience with employer account registrations (e.g., state withholding, SUI)
  • Experience filing and amending quarterly/annual payroll tax forms (e.g., 941, 940, state equivalents)
  • Familiarity with payroll platforms and systems such as ADP, Paychex, Gusto, or similar
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • High attention to detail and strong organizational skills
  • Ability to manage multiple client accounts and deadlines effectively

Why work for us

At H&R Block, our purpose is simple: to provide help and inspire confidence in our clients and communities everywhere. For more than 70 years, we’ve led the tax industry and we continue to evolve through our Block Next strategy, blending human expertise with digital innovation.

That same commitment to care extends to our associates. When you join us, you become part of a High Performing, Connected Culture built on strong relationships, continuous learning, and a shared commitment to making a meaningful impact. We invest in your well-being through competitive pay, comprehensive benefits, and support for life both in and outside of work.
Pay Range Information

The pay range for this position is listed below. Local minimum wage laws apply. This information is posted pursuant to local requirements to provide applicants with information about what they might be eligible to receive. Individual pay decisions will depend on job-related factors such as experience, education, skill, performance, and geographic location where work will be performed. Successful candidates may be able to participate in one or more incentive compensation or short-term incentive plans, which could generate additional earnings in accordance with the terms of each plan. Qualifying associates can enroll themselves and/or their eligible dependents in medical and prescription drug coverage; can participate in the H&R Block Retirement Savings Plan (401(k) Plan), the Employee Assistance Program, (virtual) fitness center programs, and the associate discount program; are automatically enrolled in Business Travel Accident Insurance; and receive Associate Tax Prep benefit.
Pay Range

$21.59 - $32.40/Hr.

jobs.title: Associate Director, K-12 (Candidates Must Reside IN INDIANA)
jobs.excerpt: Associate Director, K-12 (Candidate Must Reside in INDIANA) College Board – State & District PartnershipsLocation: This is a remote role.
jobs.description:
Associate Director, K-12 (Candidate Must Reside in INDIANA)

College Board – State & District Partnerships

Location: This is a remote role. Candidates for this role must reside in INDIANA. All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type: This is a full time position


About the Team

The Midwest Regional K-12 team at College Board is a high-performing, mission-driven consultative sales team focused on expanding access to College Board programs and services. We combine sales expertise with a deep commitment to creating opportunities for students, partnering with educators, district leaders, and state officials to drive adoption of solutions that improve student outcomes.


As part of the State & District Partnerships division, we are responsible for growing the reach and impact of College Board programs, including the SAT Suite of Assessments, Advanced Placement, and BigFuture. We take a strategic, data-informed approach to managing territories, building pipelines, and advancing opportunities from initial engagement through long-term partnership.


Our work is relationship-driven and results-oriented, with a clear focus on driving adoption and meeting ambitious growth goals across our territories. We engage in consultative sales cycles, align solutions to partner priorities, and support successful implementation to ensure sustained impact. Team members are accountable for meeting goals, continuously strengthening their sales practice, and contributing to a culture of collaboration, learning, and shared success.


About the Opportunity

As an Associate Director of K–12, you are responsible for driving growth and achieving sales goals for College Board programs and services within an assigned territory. You execute against established state and regional strategies, owning a portfolio of accounts and a pipeline of opportunities that expand access to College Board programs. Within the state and regional strategy, you own the account plans and pipeline for your territory and are accountable for the outcomes


You are accountable for driving growth and achieving sales goals for College Board programs and services within an assigned territory in Indiana and North Dakota. You lead the execution of district strategy and develop/drive the district level sales by proactively identifying opportunities, advancing conversations, and closing agreements that expand access to College Board programs, owning your pipeline from prospecting through close, and consistently advancing opportunities to drive adoption. You independently manage sales cycles and partner relationships, while collaborating with senior leaders on more complex or large-scale opportunities. Through consultative selling, strategic account management, and disciplined follow-through, you move partners from interest to commitment.


In this role, you will:


Strategic Account Planning and Sales Execution (50%)

  • Consistently build and maintain account management plans and business review with each assigned account to strengthen current program adoption and drive growth in new areas
  • Build and maintain account plans and business reviews for each assigned account, grounded in a deep understanding of state and district needs and using data to deliver customized solutions that strengthen current adoption and drive growth across your territory
  • Deeply understand state and district opportunities and challenges to deliver district account plans that provide data-driven, customized solutions to meet state and district needs, with the goal of growing business across your assigned territory
  • Track progress against goals and meet or exceed individual targets that contribute to the state- and regional-level goals of expanding post-secondary opportunities for students
  • Analyze and assess trends using College Board data sources in assigned territory, planning account activity that aligns with larger state and regional goals
  • Drive consultative, solution-based sales cycles with district leaders, influencing long-term adoption decisions.
  • Recommend territory and account prioritization to regional leadership, with supporting data and a clear rationale.
  • Produce account plans, business reviews, and district proposals that are complete and ready for use, with manager feedback refining rather than rebuilding the work.
  • Build and maintain knowledge and expertise in College Board program and service innovations as well as broader K12 educational trends
  • Test and iterate on outreach and account approaches, and bring in practices from high-performing sales organizations inside and outside College Board

Manage Key Relationships (30%)

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with key officials independently or collaboratively with colleagues while continuously identifying new opportunities to cultivate partnerships
  • Conduct necessary outreach to existing, new and previous state/district partners
  • Leverage strategic consultative discussions to plan and help conduct workshops and professional learning for K-12 constituent groups
  • Coordinate with district leadership and internal CB teams to deliver support necessary to successfully implement selected CB programs and services. Clarify goals, roles, and next steps upfront with district partners and internal teams supporting implementation

Deliver Consistent Sales Data and Insights & Projects (20%)

  • Utilize Salesforce CRM to monitor progress toward goals, account management, and opportunity management to support ongoing coaching as well as individual, regional, and divisional goal attainment
  • Share wider sales strategies, insights and innovations regionally and divisionally to accelerate CB’s growth, reach, impact and culture
  • Share effective sales practices with teammates and support newer colleagues in building their sales practice
  • Seek and apply feedback from your manager, peers, and partners on account strategy and sales approach

About You

You have:

  • You reside in the state of Indiana
  • 3–5+ years of professional experience in education, sales, or a related field. We welcome candidates with classroom teaching experience who are interested in transitioning into a consultative, goal-oriented sales role
  • Interest in and commitment to a sales career path, including comfort with owning a pipeline, meeting goals, and driving partners toward adoption decisions
  • Motivation to achieve and exceed sales goals, with a proactive approach to advancing opportunities and closing deals
  • A strong achievement orientation, with a track record of setting and attaining ambitious goals (in teaching, sales, or other performance-driven environments)
  • Ability to build and sustain meaningful relationships across diverse stakeholder groups, translating educator needs into actionable solutions and influencing partners toward adoption through consultative engagement
  • Strong organizational and prioritization skills, with the ability to manage multiple time-sensitive projects simultaneously
  • Experience using CRM systems such as Salesforce (preferred), including managing workflows and supporting data-informed decision-making
  • A Bachelor’s degree
  • Willingness to travel frequently, up to 40–50%, and maintain a valid driver’s license

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise such as live coding, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck- we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.


A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $60000-$89000.
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • This role includes a base salary plus variable compensation tied to the achievement of sales goals, with payouts on a scheduled basis. While the role is not primarily commission-driven, commissions are awarded based on performance. Performance is evaluated based on both results and behaviors, in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

Mission

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its 2025 Design Award winner for Inclusivity.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google,
leading PhD programs like Stanford, high-growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

We're looking for a Software Engineer - AI Data to join Speechify's AI team and build the data pipelines that power our model training and next-generation AI products.

We build high-quality datasets at petabyte scale and low cost by combining engineering, infrastructure, and research. We're looking for a strong software engineer who enjoys solving complex problems, exploring new data sources, and building systems that make AI training more efficient and scalable.

What You’ll Do:

  • Discover new sources of audio data and build reliable pipelines to bring them into our training datasets.
  • Build and improve large-scale data-processing systems, optimizing for data quality, throughput, and cost.
  • Collaborate closely with AI Scientists to improve training datasets and support the development of next-generation models.
  • Take ownership of engineering projects from problem discovery through implementation and continuous improvement.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have:

  • A degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, with strong backend development fundamentals.
  • Proficiency in Python and Bash in Linux environments.
  • Experience building and operating production systems, ideally involving data pipelines or large-scale data processing.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, initiative, and the ability to work independently in ambiguous environments.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with web crawlers, data acquisition, or distributed data-processing systems.
  • Experience with cloud infrastructure and Infrastructure as Code, particularly GCP and Terraform.
  • Familiarity with ML training data, dataset quality, or audio processing.

What We Offer

  • A dynamic environment where your contributions shape the company and its products
  • A team that values innovation, intuition, and drive
  • Autonomy, fostering focus and creativity
  • The opportunity to have a significant impact in a revolutionary industry
  • Competitive compensation, a welcoming atmosphere, and a commitment to an exceptional asynchronous work culture
  • The privilege of working on a product that changes lives, particularly for those with learning differences like dyslexia, ADD, and more
  • An active role at the intersection of artificial intelligence and audio – a rapidly evolving tech domain

The Bulgaria Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-55,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Paid Search
jobs.excerpt: About DarkroomDarkroom is the leading next-generation growth marketing firm engineering the brands of tomorrow.
jobs.description:
About Darkroom

Darkroom is the leading next-generation growth marketing firm engineering the brands of tomorrow. Founded in 2017, we set out to redefine what a modern agency could be, by replacing the inertia of legacy advertising behemoths with a model built for speed, intelligence, and measurable impact.

At our core, Darkroom is a human services company powered by Shadow, a universal AI commerce layer that integrates executive-level strategy with proprietary agentic technology. This fusion enables our teams to deliver outsized returns by enhancing creative output, operational efficiency, and revenue generation across every stage of the customer journey.

Our track record speaks for itself: billions in attributable revenue driven across e-commerce marketplaces, media networks, DTC ecosystems, and social commerce platforms. Every engagement feeds into our proprietary data infrastructure, enabling a continuous feedback loop that accelerates growth, improves margins, and compounds results across our client portfolio.

What began as a boutique design studio has evolved into one of the fastest-growing private companies in America (Inc. 5000) and among the most effective performance media agencies of the 2020s (Varos). Our founders were recognized by Forbes 30 Under 30 for advancing the intersection of technology, marketing, and advertising, cementing Darkroom’s role as a defining player in the future of media innovation.

About the Role

We are hiring for our Paid Media team, looking for a Senior Director, Paid Search: the head of Darkroom’s Paid Search practice. This is an executive leadership role. You’ll own the strategy, performance, and commercial health of the practice across Google, YouTube, Microsoft Advertising, and the emerging AI search ecosystem (including platforms like Perplexity, OpenAI, Koah, and Kontext as their ad products launch), lead a team of Associate Directors, Paid Search Managers, and Specialists, and be accountable for the outcomes paid search delivers across Darkroom’s client portfolio.

The ideal candidate is a recognized expert in search buying behavior who has already built and run a paid search organization. You’ve scaled Google ad accounts well beyond $1M USD per month, led teams that include people managers, and served as a trusted strategic advisor to CMOs and founders. You’re curious about where AI search is heading and want to be the person who defines how Darkroom shows up there. You think in systems, not campaigns, and you know how to build a team that runs those systems well.

You’ll report to the Managing Director of Paid Media and sit on the Paid Media leadership team, partnering with Darkroom leadership on practice growth, margin, hiring, and the evolution of our service offering. You’ll collaborate closely with Paid Social, Programmatic, Creative, Analytics, Growth Strategy, and Shadow, and will be responsible for building the next generation of paid search leaders at Darkroom.

This is a fast-paced, high-accountability environment for leaders who want to shape how a practice operates and grows. You’ll have the scope to define what best-in-class paid search looks like at Darkroom, at a moment when search itself is changing faster than it has in a decade.

Darkroom is a career incubator for ambitious talent looking to operate at the intersection of business, design, and innovation.

What you’ll do:

  • Own the multi-year vision, strategy, and performance of Darkroom’s Paid Search practice, setting the direction across traditional search, Shopping, YouTube, and AI search.

  • Sit on the Paid Media leadership team and partner with the Managing Director on practice OKRs, annual planning, budgeting, and headcount.

  • Own the practice’s commercial health, including revenue, margin, client retention, account growth, and team utilization, and report on it to Darkroom leadership.

  • Shape Darkroom’s paid search service offering, defining scopes, pricing inputs, and new service lines, including how Darkroom packages AI search as it matures.

  • Lead Paid Search’s role in new business, partnering with the Growth team on pitches, audits, and proposals, and joining final-round pitches for key prospects.

  • Build, lead, and grow a team of 6+ across Associate Directors, Paid Search Managers, and Specialists, with Associate Directors and Specialists reporting directly to you.

  • Develop the practice’s leadership bench, coaching your Associate Directors into strong people managers, growing Specialists into future leaders, and building succession plans for every leadership seat.

  • Own the practice’s org design and hiring plan in partnership with Recruiting, from leveling and role definition to final hiring decisions on leadership roles.

  • Set career paths, leveling expectations, and the performance review process for the practice, and ensure every team member has an individualized growth plan.

  • Build a culture of accountability, craft, and candor where high performers want to stay and grow.

  • Serve as executive sponsor for Darkroom’s largest and most strategic Paid Search relationships, leading executive business reviews and annual planning with CMOs, founders, and leadership teams.

  • Act as the final escalation point for high-stakes client and performance issues, and own retention strategy for at-risk accounts across the practice.

  • Own key platform partner relationships with Google and Microsoft, securing beta access, support, and early insight for Darkroom clients.

  • Lead Darkroom’s AI search build-out, tracking and piloting new ad products as they launch, defining how the team tests them, and making Darkroom the go-to voice for clients on where search is heading.

  • Represent Darkroom’s paid search point of view externally through industry events, content, and partner programs.

  • Partner with Shadow’s product team to shape the AI and agentic tooling the practice runs on, and drive adoption so the team becomes more efficient and more effective at scale.

  • Set the standards for campaign architecture, bidding strategy, optimization frameworks, and testing methodology across a portfolio of 15+ accounts with aggregate monthly spend of $3M to $10M+.

  • Own the practice’s Shopping and Performance Max standards, including feed quality and Merchant Center best practices.

  • Define the creative standard for the practice, including ad copy, landing page alignment, and short-form video for YouTube, and make sure it’s applied consistently across every account.

  • Lead the practice’s measurement approach in partnership with Analytics, including attribution, incrementality testing, brand search cannibalization testing, and media mix modeling, and set the KPI framework (CPA, CAC, iROAS, nCAC, MER, aMER, CTR, and CPM) every account is held to.

  • Turn learnings from across the portfolio into repeatable playbooks, and stay close enough to the work to audit accounts, spot issues early, and lead by example.

What you’ll need to be successful:

  • 10+ years of paid media advertising experience, with at least 8+ years specializing in Paid Search and Google in particular.

  • 5+ years leading paid search teams, including 3+ years managing managers, with experience leading a team of 6+ in a fast-paced agency or in-house environment.

  • Proven experience building or scaling a paid search practice or department, including org design, hiring, process, and service delivery standards.

  • Experience owning or directly influencing a practice or department P&L, including revenue, margin, utilization, and pricing.

  • Track record of overseeing paid search portfolios at $3M+ in aggregate monthly spend, and of personally scaling Google ad accounts beyond $1M USD/month while maintaining or improving efficiency.

  • Executive presence with CMOs, founders, and internal leadership: ability to build trust, present strategic recommendations with confidence, and navigate complex stakeholder dynamics.

  • Expert-level command of Google Ads, including Shopping, Performance Max, and YouTube, and deep familiarity with Microsoft Advertising and the emerging AI search ad ecosystem.

  • Mastery of the e-commerce marketing funnel, from offer to ad to landing page to conversion.

  • Mastery of e-commerce performance metrics (CPA, CAC, iROAS, nCAC, MER, aMER, CTR, CPM) and modern measurement approaches, including incrementality and brand search cannibalization testing.

  • Strong background in portfolio-level budget forecasting, spend projection modeling, and data-derived decision-making.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; able to distill complex data into compelling insights for teams, clients, and Darkroom leadership.

What It's Like to Work at Darkroom

Darkroom is not a typical agency. We are looking for A players who want to build something great. We move fast, think deeply, and expect every team member to bring insight and rigor to everything they touch. We hold a high bar for performance, creativity, and ownership — but we also support each other relentlessly. No egos, no red tape — just world-class talent building something remarkable.

We believe in autonomy with accountability, truth over comfort, and outcomes over optics.

  • Unlimited PTO + US holidays: Rebooting is part of the work. Take the time you need to stay sharp.

  • Remote-First Culture: Many roles are fully remote. Employees based in or near our New York or Lisbon HQs are expected to work hybrid with weekly in-office time. Hub locations include Brazil and Spain.

  • Health & Wellness: Company-sponsored medical, dental, and vision coverage.

  • Finances, growth, and retirement: Darkroom offers a robust 401(k) program with company match and profit-sharing opportunities to help you save and grow as the company grows.

  • Parental Leave: Flexible parental leave to support new parents during this important transition.

  • Growth: Our interdisciplinary model gives every Darkroomer exposure far beyond their core role. Grow your skills, expand your influence, and stay at the forefront of the industry.

Equal Opportunity Statement

Darkroom is an equal opportunity workplace—we are dedicated to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national orientation, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.

jobs.title: Accounting Manager — AI & Automation
jobs.excerpt: Are you an accounting leader who is obsessed with AI?
jobs.description:
Are you an accounting leader who is obsessed with AI?

We're looking for an experienced accountant who believes AI is going to fundamentally change how accounting gets done — and wants to be at the forefront of that transformation. Arboreal manages more than 10,000 apartments, and we've built our own property-management software platform, Maynard, with extensive APIs and MCP tools that let AI agents work directly in our accounting systems. This role is your chance to prove how much more a great accountant can accomplish when the manual work is handed to AI and the judgment stays with you.

The Role

This is a new kind of accounting role, built for how Arboreal intends to run its accounting function going forward. Rather than managing a team of people, the Accounting Manager oversees the accounting for a book of work primarily through AI agents operating on Maynard in conjunction with AppFolio. The focus is judgment and review: directing and supervising automated workflows, tackling complex reconciliations and investigations with AI, preparing and reviewing journal entries, validating what the agents produce, and standing behind the accuracy of the financials. You'll be one of four Accounting Managers who work side by side to make sure financials go out on time and accurately and that balances are reconciled across the portfolio. A shared pool of accountants performs a limited set of manual tasks and AI-assisted supporting reconciliations; these accountants do not report to this role. You'll have direct access to the CFO, the engineering team, and our AI-enabled accounting tools — and you'll be encouraged to experiment, improve processes, and figure out how much more is possible. This position reports directly to the Chief Financial Officer and spans accounts payable and receivable, corporate accounting, client onboarding and offboarding, and the review of property financials.

Oversee Accounting Through AI Agents & Automation

  • Own the accounting for an assigned book of work, executed primarily through AI agents running on Maynard alongside AppFolio — directing, supervising, and quality-controlling their output rather than performing each task by hand.
  • Use AI to tackle complex reconciliations, investigate accounting problems, and automate work that traditionally takes hours of manual effort.
  • Prepare and review journal entries and reconciliations, and review AI- and system-generated entries and reports for accuracy, completeness, proper coding, and compliance with U.S. GAAP before they are relied upon.
  • Identify, investigate, and resolve exceptions the agents flag or that review surfaces, and determine when a human needs to step in.
  • Experiment with and improve agent workflows, prompts, rules, and controls — partnering with the CFO and engineering team so the system produces reliable results and keeps getting better.
  • Act as a knowledgeable check on automation — understanding what the agents are doing well enough to catch when an output is wrong, and never signing off on numbers that have not been verified.

Timely & Accurate Financial Reporting

  • Work alongside the other three Accounting Managers to ensure financial statements go out on time and accurately for the assigned portfolio each period.
  • Coordinate the close calendar and hand-offs across the manager group so there are no gaps or duplicated work, and so dependencies are met.
  • Support monthly, quarterly, and annual close and produce financials in accordance with U.S. GAAP.
  • Provide the CFO with variance explanations, supporting schedules, and management reporting for lenders, owners, and external tax preparers and auditors.

Reconciliations & Balance Integrity

  • Ensure balance-sheet accounts are reconciled and that balances are supported, reviewing the AI-assisted reconciliations prepared on the platform and by the accountant pool.
  • Confirm that AP and AR subledgers tie to the general ledger, and that cash, prepaids, accrued liabilities, intercompany, and interproperty balances are clean before financials are issued.
  • Investigate and clear aged, unapplied, or exception items, and document the resolution so it can be reviewed and audited.

Functional Areas Overseen

Across the following areas, the Accounting Manager owns the quality and timeliness of the work — exercised through the platform, the AI agents, and the shared accountant pool — and provides the review and sign-off:

  • Accounts Payable & Accounts Receivable — oversight of invoice processing, payment runs, billings, receipts, and the related reconciliations, with controls over approvals, segregation of duties, and payment authorization.
  • Corporate Accounting — oversight of the management-company entities' close, including accruals, prepaids, intercompany activity, account reconciliations, and corporate financial statements.
  • Client Onboarding & Offboarding — oversight of the accounting workstream when properties and clients come on board or depart: opening balances, chart-of-accounts mapping and setup in AppFolio, final reconciliations, balance transfers, and clean handoff of records.
  • Property Financials Review — review of property financial statements for assigned portfolios before they reach owners, checking for abnormal balances, misclassifications, and unreconciled items.

What We're Looking For

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance (or equivalent professional experience), and solid accounting experience with a strong grasp of general ledgers, reconciliations, and financial statements.
  • Strong working knowledge of U.S. GAAP and U.S. accounting practices, including accruals, reconciliations, and month-end close.
  • Hands-on experience with AppFolio (property-management accounting) — transacting, configuring, and reporting within the platform.
  • Real enthusiasm for AI tools — Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, or similar — and a belief that technology changes what an accountant can do.
  • An analytical mindset and willingness to learn SQL, APIs, and automation. You don't need to be a programmer — you do need to get excited about making a computer do something that used to take all afternoon.
  • Strong review judgment — able to look at an output and tell whether it's right, and to find the error when it isn't.
  • Ability to work independently, take ownership of complex accounting problems, and deliver results through systems and coordination rather than a direct-report team.
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication and the ability to coordinate with a U.S.-based leadership team and peer managers.
  • Ability to work remotely from the Philippines with dependable internet and regular overlap with U.S. Pacific business hours.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in U.S. property management, real estate, or multi-entity accounting environments.
  • CPA (Philippines or U.S.) or equivalent professional certification.
  • Experience with accounting automation, RPA, or AI tooling, or working on a proprietary or custom accounting system.
  • Experience onboarding new properties/entities or converting balances from a prior accounting system.
  • Comfort working across multiple AppFolio databases/tenants.

Engagement Terms

This is an independent contractor (1099) engagement, not an offer of employment. Services are provided remotely from the Philippines, and working hours are coordinated with the CFO to support timely month-end close and reporting. As an independent contractor, the individual is responsible for their own taxes and will provide a completed Form W-8BEN. Compensation and start date are addressed separately in the engagement letter.

jobs.description:
About DrFirst

For 25 years, DrFirst has empowered providers and patients to achieve better health through intelligent medication management. We improve healthcare workflows and help patients start and stay on therapy with end-to-end solutions that enhance prescription access, affordability, and adherence. Our solutions help 100 million patients a year and are used by more than 420,000 prescribers, 71,000 pharmacies, 270 EHRs and health information systems, and over 2,000 hospitals in the U.S. This is a great opportunity to be a part of a successful Healthcare IT company experiencing significant growth. Here you'll get to work with some of the smartest and most interesting people around; solving unique and complex challenges in healthcare on a scale matched by a few companies. If you get excited about stretching yourself in new ways, developing yourself to your fullest potential, care about working with smart colleagues; we want to talk to you!

Position Overview

DrFirst is building an agentic ecosystem at scale. In the last 90 days we have shipped production AI systems across HR, Finance, Legal, and Marketing, automating hundreds of hours of manual work monthly and delivering measurable business impact.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You architect and build production AI automation systems from discovery to deployment. You work directly with department leaders to map workflows and ship tools that augment their work.

The split is 80% individual-contributor engineering and 20% servant leadership and mentorship. You build. You own technical architecture decisions. As the team scales from 2 to 5-6 engineers over 18 months, you mentor through code review and pairing. You also teach non-technical department leaders how to use AI tools, translate technical concepts for executives, and run discovery sessions that extract workflows from stakeholders. Building stays your primary focus.

Who Will Love This Job

  • You are a senior IC who loves shipping code daily. You have been a Staff or Principal Engineer or led small teams, but you miss hands-on building.
  • You can architect multi-agent systems and run discovery sessions with department VPs to map their workflows.
  • You can debug OAuth2 flows through enterprise proxies and explain security requirements to non-technical stakeholders.
  • You are a servant leader. You remove blockers for others, teach through pairing rather than directives, and make stakeholders successful.
  • You organize chaos: 15 stakeholders, 6 systems, 3 sprints in flight. You ask “How can I help?” before “Here is what you should do.”

What you will work on

Build Production AI Automation (80%)

You own the technical implementation of department sprints. Example: an HR sprint delivered resume screening (40-candidate PDF extraction with table-of-contents parsing and fuzzy name matching), OKR coaching (Leapsome API integration with performance rating analytics), performance ratings (calibration detection across 328 employees), and milestone email automation in 4 weeks.

  • Architecture and Implementation: Design and build Python/FastAPI backends connecting to enterprise APIs (HRIS, ERP, CRM, finance systems, project management).
  • Frontend Development: Build Next.js/React frontends with Okta SSO, role-based access control, and audit trails.
  • Multi-Agent Systems: Design agent coordination systems, skill discovery hubs, agent registries, and workflow orchestration.
  • Enterprise Integration: Navigate Zscaler proxies, VPNs, SSL certificates, Kubernetes pod networking, DynamoDB, and AWS Bedrock.
  • Testing and Quality: Write Playwright end-to-end tests before production deploy and maintain a 1000+ test suite with visual regression baselines.
  • Deployment: Ship via GitLab CI/CD to AWS EKS (Kubernetes, ArgoCD, Helm, Secrets Manager) and diagnose pod restarts and liveness probe issues.
  • Async and Performance: Debug event loop blocking, convert synchronous I/O to async, and optimize CPU-bound operations.
  • Security: Partner with the CISO on PII/PHI de-identification, least privilege, and per-user OAuth2.
  • Production Support: Debug authentication flows, token expiration, API rate limits, and health check failures.

You will ship 3-5 production tools in parallel within each sprint, deploying multiple times per day based on stakeholder feedback.

Servant Leadership and Mentorship (20%)

Guide 2-3 engineers through code reviews and pairing. Teach department leaders how to use AI tools effectively. Translate technical decisions for non-technical executives. No direct reports and no performance reviews. Pure servant leadership.

  • Technical Mentorship: Code reviews, pairing sessions, and unblocking complex integrations.
  • Non-Technical Teaching: Run discovery sessions with department VPs, teach Finance/HR/Legal leaders how to prompt AI tools, and build interfaces non-technical users can modify.
  • Stakeholder Translation: Explain security trade-offs to executives and translate “OAuth2 delegation” into “everyone sees only their own data.”
  • Remove Blockers: Clear obstacles for team members, escalate infrastructure issues, and coordinate across departments.
  • Knowledge Sharing: Document patterns so others can self-serve and write playbooks department heads can follow without engineering help.

Daily Work

  • Morning sync with the VP of AI Automation on build queue, blockers, and technical decisions.
  • Direct coordination with 15+ stakeholders across departments.
  • Discovery sessions with department leaders to map workflows.
  • Hands-on coding: backend services, frontend components, and integration tests.
  • Security reviews with the CISO.
  • Ship multiple times per day and debug production issues.
  • Code reviews for 2-3 team members.

Qualifications

Required

  • 8+ years building production systems end-to-end (backend, frontend, integrations, infrastructure).
  • Staff/Principal Engineer or Tech Lead experience, owning technical decisions on production systems.

Senior Media & External Corporate Communications Manager

Location: Remote UK based, able to travel to our Head Office in London and other operational sites around the UK when required

As Media & External Corporate Communications Manager, you will play a crucial role in managing a busy press office, media relations and issues management at the heart of the role. You will lead and support responses to complex and high-profile media enquiries, working across the business to protect Capita’s reputation. Alongside this, you will help proactively build our profile and communicate Capita’s transformation narrative to key external stakeholders through national media (including broadcast), regional press, trade press, owned social media and digital channels. Our clients and prospects are primarily public sector organisations, alongside some large private companies, and our work often directly affects the individuals and communities who rely on essential services.

You will report to our Head of External Communications and Marketing, and will work closely with our internal communications team, contract communications teams and marketing teams, as well as liaising closely with investor relations, public affairs and external communications agencies.

Successful candidates must have experience from a PR agency background and journalism.

At Capita, we live by our values: 🤝 Customer First, Always; 🧑‍💻 Fearless Innovation; ✅ Achieve Together; 💙 Everyone is Valued. These guide how we work, collaborate, and deliver exceptional results.

Job title:

Senior Media and External Corporate Communications Manager

Job Description:

What you’ll be doing

  • Managing and responding to daily media enquiries, often involving complex, high-profile or sensitive issues that affect individuals and communities.
  • Identifying emerging reputational risks and working with contract communications leads, public affairs, internal communications, legal teams, senior leaders and external PR agencies to agree clear handling and escalation plans.
  • Developing reactive statements, lines to take, Q&As, briefing materials and other communications needed to support rapid and accurate responses.
  • Providing clear, evidence-based communications advice to senior leaders, including constructive challenge where required, and preparing spokespeople for interviews and difficult questions.
  • Supporting crisis communications planning and urgent issues outside normal working hours when required.
  • Helping to shape and deliver Capita’s external communications strategy and plan.
  • Developing credible stories and campaigns that demonstrate Capita’s transformation, expertise and contribution to the delivery of essential public services across earned, owned, social and digital channels.
  • Working closely with colleagues across contracts and functions to identify evidence, insight, case studies and spokespeople that strengthen our external narrative.
  • Building trusted relationships with reporters at key national and trade media outlets covering Capita and the sectors in which we operate.
  • Monitoring the media, business and UK political landscape to anticipate risks and identify opportunities to share informed viewpoints and profile our spokespeople.
  • Monitoring coverage and evaluating communications activity, using insight and evidence to improve future plans and report on reputation, reach and impact.

What we’re looking for -

Essential Skills & Experience

  • Proven experience in corporate communications within a PR agency, including media relations and issues management involving UK national and trade media.
  • Journalism experience, with a strong understanding of how the media operates and what makes a good story.
  • Experience of communications within the public sector, regulated industries or another complex and highly scrutinised environment is preferable.

Bright Vision Technologies is a technology consulting and software development company delivering cloud, AI, data, and enterprise solutions across the United States.
