Experience Required: 6+ years

Sponsorship: U.S. Citizens, Green Card Holders, EAD Holders, and H-1B transfer candidates are encouraged to apply. We are unable to sponsor new H-1B visa petitions for this position.

Job Summary
We are seeking an experienced PeopleSoft Integration Broker Developer to design, build, and operate enterprise integrations connecting PeopleSoft applications to internal systems, cloud applications, and third-party platforms. This role focuses specifically on the integration layer, including service operations, queues, routings, transformations, security configurations, and error handling. The ideal candidate will combine deep hands-on Integration Broker experience with broader PeopleTools knowledge and a strong understanding of API and integration design patterns. In this role you will work closely with cross-functional partners — product, design, engineering, operations, and business stakeholders — to translate ambiguous requirements into well-engineered solutions, and will be expected to raise the bar through code review, design review, and mentorship of more junior engineers. The successful candidate brings strong engineering discipline, a clear communication style, and a track record of shipping meaningful work that holds up well in production.

Key Responsibilities
  • Design and develop integration scenarios using PeopleSoft Integration Broker, including service operations, queues, routings, and handlers.
  • Build synchronous and asynchronous integrations using REST and SOAP web services.
  • Develop transformations using XSLT, Application Engine, and PeopleCode handlers, applying disciplined engineering practices and partnering closely with stakeholders to ensure outcomes are durable, well-documented, and aligned with broader team and platform standards.
  • Configure security on inbound and outbound services, including WS-Security, OAuth2, and certificate-based authentication.
  • Build robust error-handling and retry mechanisms, including notifications, monitoring, and resubmission workflows.
  • Develop Component Interfaces and File Layouts to support hybrid integration scenarios.
  • Lead migration efforts to retire legacy point-to-point integrations to standardized Integration Broker patterns, planning phased cutovers, building backward-compatibility shims where needed, and ensuring each migration step is reversible and well-monitored.
  • Optimize performance of high-volume integrations through queue tuning, parallel processing, and asynchronous design.
  • Integrate PeopleSoft with cloud applications (Oracle Cloud, Workday, ServiceNow) and middleware (OIC, MuleSoft, Boomi).
  • Maintain comprehensive, current technical documentation — including architecture diagrams, design decisions, configuration references, runbooks, and operational procedures — so that the system remains supportable, auditable, and easy to onboard new engineers onto over time.
  • Provide hypercare and post-go-live support, including incident response and root-cause analysis.
  • Collaborate closely with functional consultants and integration architects, gathering requirements, aligning on technical approach, and ensuring that delivered solutions meet both functional needs and broader engineering and operational standards.
  • Mentor and coach junior and mid-level engineers through code review, design review, pair programming, and structured knowledge sharing, helping the broader team grow in technical maturity and confidence over time.
Required Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Five or more years of PeopleSoft development experience, with a strong focus on Integration Broker.
  • Hands-on experience designing and developing REST and SOAP web services in PeopleSoft.
  • Solid PeopleCode and Application Engine experience.
  • Working knowledge of XML, XSLT, and JSON.
  • Experience with web service security standards (WS-Security, OAuth2).
  • Strong SQL skills and experience with the PeopleSoft data model.
  • Familiarity with middleware platforms (OIC, MuleSoft, Boomi) is a strong plus.
  • Excellent troubleshooting, communication, and documentation skills.
  • Experience supporting PeopleSoft upgrades and patches.
Preferred Qualifications
  • PeopleSoft certifications.
  • Experience integrating with Oracle Cloud Applications.
  • Exposure to event-driven integration patterns.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD tooling for PeopleSoft.
  • Strong understanding of API management concepts.

Senior Counsel, Commercial Transactions (TPA)

Ready to close the deals that power self-funded health plans?

Behind every self-funded employer plan we administer sits a web of contracts, and those contracts decide how fast we can move, how well we serve plan sponsors, and how confidently we stand behind our promises. As Senior Counsel on Personify Health’s commercial legal team, you’ll build the agreements that make our TPA business work, from client administrative services agreements to the network, pharmacy, stop-loss, and vendor partnerships behind them. You’ll partner directly with Sales, Account Management, Operations, Finance, and Procurement, giving them clear, practical legal guidance that keeps deals compliant and moving. Reporting to the SVP, Legal, you’ll run your own practice and own your transactions from first draft to signature. When your contracts are sharp and your counsel is trusted, our teams win business faster and our members get the care and coverage they count on.

jobs.title: Financial Controller - Remote - Independent Contractor - PH Based
jobs.excerpt: Living in a Bubble sells premium campervan and outdoor accessories, direct to consumers and through marketplaces in Australia, the United States, Canada and Germany.
jobs.description:
Living in a Bubble sells premium campervan and outdoor accessories, direct to consumers and through marketplaces in Australia, the United States, Canada and Germany. We operate across two legal entities and five tax jurisdictions. We are a team of fourteen — two in Australia, twelve working remotely across the Philippines and elsewhere. We are small, run properly, and our bookkeeping is handled by an external firm. What we do not have is a finance professional who owns the output.

Right now the CEO does all of the finance: the monthly close, five indirect tax regimes, the pricing analysis, the landed cost, the advisor coordination. It works, and it does not scale, and there is no one else who could pick it up.

You would take that. Not the bookkeeping — an external firm does the bookkeeping. The layer above it: whether the numbers are right, whether the filings are on time, and whether someone other than the founder can read the business.

This is a build-and-run role in a business that has never had one. You will inherit real processes that mostly work and real gaps that do not. You bring the analysis and the judgement; the CEO keeps the final call on pricing, payments, tax and structure.

What you would own

  1. The monthly close. You own the calendar, the quality bar and the query queue while the external bookkeeper does the execution. Settlement reconciliation for two marketplace accounts, the consolidated group P&L across both entities, the stock take, and the year-end pack for our Australian tax advisors. Getting the close to business day five is a first-half objective, not a week-one expectation.
  2. Indirect tax in five jurisdictions. US sales tax, German VAT, UK VAT under Making Tax Digital, Canadian GST, Australian BAS. Four external firms do the filings. You are not expected to have technical depth in all five regimes — nobody does. You run the control that sits over them: a filing calendar nobody misses, data prepared to each firm's specification, a reconciliation of what was filed against what the books say, and a written query log when the two disagree.
  3. Management reporting. Daily channel P&L across both marketplace accounts, a weekly sales report, a monthly P&L analysis with an executive summary someone acts on, the KPI scorecard, product and range performance. Today these exist in pieces; you would make them one thing.
  4. Pricing and unit economics. The standing price review, margin verification after every price change, markdowns on aged stock, contribution by channel, third-party logistics cost against what we are charged. You bring the analysis; the CEO decides.
  5. Landed cost. A monthly reference refresh and verification of cost uploads. Cost rolls forward in our systems, so an error corrupts forward margin silently and nothing tells you. There is a backlog of known cost conflicts to work through in your first half-year.
  6. Controls and documentation. A written SOP for every recurring process, an access map so the function survives any one person being unavailable, and an audit-readiness file that does not exist today. These are gating deliverables, not nice-to-haves.

Not in this role

Payment release stays with the CEO. Accounts payable processing and payroll preparation stay where they are today, with our EA and the external bookkeeper, so your time goes to the close, the tax control, the reporting and the analysis. As the function grows, a finance assistant will take on that transactional layer and report to you.

Your first 90 days

  1. Month 1. Access to everything, mapped and documented. Take over the daily and weekly reporting. Sit through one full close and write down what actually happens, as opposed to what is supposed to. Inherit the filing calendar and confirm two quarters of deadlines.
  2. Month 2. Own the close on its current timetable, fully documented, and give us a dated plan to bring it forward to business day five. Produce the consolidated group P&L without the CEO involved. Run the landed-cost refresh end to end. Write your first three SOPs.
  3. Month 3. The monthly pack lands without being asked for. The filing calendar runs itself. The CEO reads exceptions rather than reports.
  4. Month 6. Close at business day five with variance inside tolerance. The SOP set and access map complete. First formal review.

Beyond that, year one is about the things nobody has had time to settle: the FX convention, the product identifier gaps, a costed recommendation on US state tax registration, and discount bands with margin floors so that marketing can approve inside a band.

Where this role goes

We would rather you understood the arc than discovered it.

Months 0 to 6 — you take the machine off the founder. The recurring reporting, the close, the filing calendar. Success here is measured in the CEO's calendar, not in anything you build. It is the least interesting phase and the one that earns everything after it.

Months 6 to 18 — Controller proper. The judgement work starts: the FX convention, SKU mapping across our largest channel, landed-cost integrity, a costed position on US state registration, discount bands the business runs inside. This is where you stop producing reports and start producing answers.

Months 18 onward — the role splits in two directions and you will have a say in which. One path is Head of Finance, with a finance assistant beneath you taking the transactional layer, then forecasting, inventory-buy modelling and planning. The other is transaction readiness: audit-ready accounts, quality of earnings, normalised reporting, a data room. Both are real, and the review at month six is where we start that conversation rather than the first place we surprise you with it.

What will not change: payment release and the final call on pricing, structure and tax sit with the CEO.

How you will be checked

You are the finance function, so the quality control is external by design and we would rather be explicit about it. Our external bookkeeping firm checks the work at the close. Our Australian tax advisors check it annually at year-end. You are not being asked to be your own second pair of eyes, and nobody here expects a clean run with no queries.

Requirements

  1. CPA or CA qualified, with a Big 4 audit or advisory background at manager or assistant manager level, or equivalent depth in industry.
  2. Multi-entity, multi-currency reporting — consolidating entities with different start dates, and a defensible view on how FX should be handled.
  3. Close discipline — calendar, working papers, reconciliations, variance tolerance, and the temperament to hold an external bookkeeper to a standard.
  4. Indirect tax across more than one jurisdiction. Not all five of ours, but you have coordinated external firms and you know what a control over an outsourced filing looks like.
  5. Comfortable building before you delegate. In year one you build it and you also run it.
  6. Writing. A good half of this job is an executive summary that someone reads and acts on.
  7. Based in the Philippines, able to work as an independent contractor, with a daily availability window overlapping the Australian morning.

Useful, not required

E-commerce or consumer goods; Power BI or similar modelling; inventory-heavy businesses and landed-cost work; Australian tax exposure.

We expect to teach you

Our marketplace analytics stack, settlement journals and fee mechanics, our SKU conventions, and an inventory system that is mid-implementation. Nobody arrives knowing these, and not knowing them is not a reason to hold back an application.

Benefits

  • Generous remuneration depending on experience, invoiced monthly in US dollars.
  • An annual bonus arrangement in line with the rest of our remote team.
  • Fully remote, with an agreed daily availability window rather than fixed office hours.
  • A formal review at six months covering performance, conversion to a permanent arrangement, and whether the scope of the role widens.
  • A defined path beyond year one — Head of Finance with a team beneath you, or transaction readiness. You would have a say in which.
  • Direct reporting line to the CEO. No layer between your analysis and the decision.
  • External assurance by design: our bookkeeping firm checks the work at each close and our Australian tax advisors check it annually, so you are not the only pair of eyes on your own output.

The Opportunity

Make an Impact on Complex Construction Projects

We're looking for an experienced Project Scheduler who enjoys being at the center of project planning and execution. In this role, you'll work closely with project managers, engineers, and construction teams to analyze schedules to help keep projects moving forward, identify potential risks before they become issues for owners, and provide the insights needed to make critical project decisions.

This is an excellent opportunity for a scheduler who has worked on the contractor side of the business and understands the realities of construction project delivery. You'll be part of a collaborative team, contribute to high-profile projects, and have the opportunity to influence project success from planning through completion.

The ideal candidate brings 5-10 years of construction scheduling experience, strong expertise with Primavera P6, and the ability to turn project data into meaningful reporting through Power BI. Experience with contractor-driven projects is highly valued. The internal job description also identifies Primavera P6 as a core scheduling tool for this role.

Responsibilities include but aren't limited to:

  • Review detailed construction schedules against project specifications to support successful project delivery.
  • Partner with project teams to understand scope, sequencing, milestones, and schedule requirements.
  • Analyze project schedules to identify critical path activities, risks, opportunities, and potential delays.
  • Track project progress and provide forecasting to help teams proactively manage schedule performance.
  • Collaborate with procurement and construction teams to ensure actual dates, material lead times and key project milestones are accurately reflected.
  • Create meaningful reports and dashboards that provide visibility into project performance and schedule health.
  • Use Primavera P6 and Power BI to support planning, reporting, and project controls efforts.
  • Communicate schedule updates and recommendations clearly to project teams and stakeholders.

To be successful in this role, you will have:

  • Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Civil Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 5-10 years of construction scheduling experience.
  • Experience working for a general contractor, heavy civil contractor, or construction contractor.
  • Strong proficiency with Primavera P6 and experience managing complex construction schedules. The job description specifically lists P6 experience as a key requirement.
  • Experience using Power BI to create reports, dashboards, and project performance metrics.
  • Strong understanding of Critical Path Method (CPM) scheduling, forecasting, and schedule analysis.
  • Excellent analytical, organizational, problem-solving and technical writing skills.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to build relationships across project teams and stakeholders.

You’ll stand out with:

  • Heavy construction project experience.
  • Experience creating and maintaining CPM schedules on large, complex programs.
  • Experience supporting large, complex construction programs.
  • Experience performing schedule forecasting, delay analysis, or forensic schedule reviews.
  • Experience creating executive-level reporting and visual dashboards.
  • Experience supporting project controls teams.

Why Join Us?

This role offers the opportunity to work on challenging and meaningful construction projects while partnering with industry professionals who are passionate about delivering exceptional results. Your expertise will directly influence project planning, decision-making, and overall project success.

If you enjoy solving complex scheduling challenges, working closely with project teams, and using data to drive better outcomes, we'd love to hear from you.

An Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability.

While RS&H was founded in 1941, we have been providing construction management services as one of our primary business practices since 1984. RS&H’s Transportation-Construction Management Practice serves numerous state departments of transportation, mobility/transportation authorities, turnpike/toll authorities, rail/port authorities, municipal/county governments, and private clients throughout the United States. Our Construction Engineering and Inspections (CEI) teams as well as our Construction Management teams are industry leading experts who provide a full range of construction engineering, program management, specialized testing, and inspection services from the preconstruction phase through maintenance and operations. By joining our team, you too can provide unique expertise in the full life cycle of transportation delivery, and lead the evolution of transportation.

Employee-owned, RS&H is one of the nation’s leading architecture, engineering, and consulting firms, with associates who work hard every day to create tomorrow together. We offer an exceptional journey from start to future. Our integrated teams translate experience into insight, turn challenges into opportunities, and build relationships that are as strong as the buildings and infrastructure we deliver together. We attribute our success to our unwavering commitment to our core values: integrity, accountability, curiosity, and teamwork.

Position Overview

This role is responsible for leading the product vision, roadmap, prioritization, and lifecycle management of

maintenance, data engineering, MLOps, and software engineering teams to translate manufacturing

challenges into practical, scalable AI products. Because this role sets technical direction and supports the

growth of an engineering team, hands-on experience building AI, ML, computer vision, or software

solutions is strongly preferred.

Capability Alignment

This role is aligned to the AI Automation & Enablement pillar and owns or contributes to the following

enterprise capabilities:

  • Computer Vision & Edge AI
  • Agentic & Autonomous Systems
  • Machine Learning & Predictive Analytics

Key Responsibilities

Product Vision & Roadmap

  • Define and maintain the product roadmap for assigned AI capability domains, prioritizing use cases
  • with operations and business sponsors and ensuring alignment with Novelis' enterprise AI strategy,
  • manufacturing priorities, and measurable business value.
  • Conduct use case discovery, feasibility assessment, and business value analysis to identify and
  • prioritize the highest-impact AI automation opportunities across the global manufacturing footprint.

  • criteria, and release plans, balancing delivery speed with quality, governance, and long-term
  • supportability.
  • Own the product backlog and full lifecycle from concept through production deployment, monitoring,
  • and continuous improvement, providing visibility into progress, risks, dependencies, and trade-offs.

Stakeholder Partnership & Delivery

  • Partner with plant operations, quality, safety, maintenance, and business stakeholders to translate
  • operational pain points into deployable, governed AI solutions that drive measurable improvements.
  • Communicate product vision, roadmap progress, delivery timelines, and trade-offs to senior leadership
  • and cross-functional partners.

  • dependencies, standards, ownership, and readiness, and with MLOps for production deployment and
  • monitoring requirements.

Strategic Traceability & Enterprise Alignment

  • reliability, metal flow optimization, 3×30 sustainability goals, and cash focus/operational efficiency.

  • workflows and deliverables.

This role directly manages a team of developers and is accountable for both product outcomes and team

performance, growth, and engagement, specifically:

  • responsible delivery, balancing speed, quality, governance, and long-term supportability.

IT owns the AI systems, their engineering, operation, and guardrails; operations and business partners

own the business rules, thresholds, and decisions those systems execute. This role does not own core

data platforms, ingestion pipelines, business KPI definitions, performance reporting dashboards, data

governance rules, MDM policy, or data access configuration.

About Medefer

Medefer is a pioneer in virtual-first specialist healthcare. Founded by NHS consultants over a decade ago, we were delivering consultant-led virtual outpatient care well before “virtual hospitals” became a national priority. Our model has since been cited in government and NHS England material on the NHS Online vision as one of the service models informing this direction.

We sit at the intersection of clinical provider and technology company. Our CQC-registered service is powered by Medefer’s own electronic health record and referral platform, connecting GPs, consultants, diagnostic providers and hospitals into a single coordinated system. This approach has won multiple national awards for elective recovery, innovation and impact, and we now serve both NHS partners and private patients across the UK.

Medefer is built on three principles: innovate to solve real system problems, collaborate with clinicians and partners, and put patients first in every decision. As we scale across Integrated Care Systems and grow our private services, joining now means helping to define what modern specialist care looks like - and owning the financial strategy behind it.

About the role: Consultant Psychiatrist

Location: Fully remote
Contract: Self-employed
Working pattern: Flexible, agreed sessions
Rates: Competitive sessional rates

You will deliver thorough, evidence-based adult ADHD assessments, making diagnostic decisions and providing clear reports and personalised recommendations. Your approach will be compassionate and neuroaffirmative, recognising each person’s strengths, needs and lived experience.

This is a fully remote role, and due to the nature of the role you must have a private and secure space from which to work with reliable internet access.

KeyResponsibilities

  • Conducting remote adult ADHD assessments using DSM-5 diagnostic criteria, structured assessment tools, clinical judgement and NICE guidance.

  • Reviewing referral information, relevant records, developmental history and collateral information to understand symptoms and their impact across settings.

  • Assessing differential diagnoses, coexisting conditions and clinical risk, seeking further information or specialist input where needed.

  • Confirming informed consent, considering capacity where indicated and assessing suitability for remote consultation.

  • Identifying and responding to safeguarding concerns and urgent clinical risks.

  • Explaining diagnostic outcomes sensitively, including uncertainty or when ADHD criteria are not met, and recommending appropriate next steps.

  • Producing accurate diagnostic reports and outcome letters within agreed timescales, communicating with patients, GPs and other professionals as appropriate.

  • Contributing to multidisciplinary working, clinical governance, audit, quality assurance and peer review.

About You:

You will be:

  • A Consultant Psychiatrist with NHS experience

  • Registered with the GMC with a licence to practice.

  • On the Specialist Register and be able to provide current documents in accordance with clinical competence requirements.

  • Have demonstrable training and experience in assessing and diagnosing ADHD in adults.

  • Have an interest in digital health, clinical informatics and in new ways of working.

  • Have exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, both verbal and written.

  • Possess excellent time management, planning, and prioritising skills.

  • Be detail oriented, able to process detailed information effectively, consistently, and accurately.

The resume writer will create strategy-driven career marketing documents—resumes, cover letters, and LinkedIn profiles—highlighting our clients' skills, experience, and accomplishments. This person will have a keen eye for detail and be very comfortable conducting independent research on each client's job function within healthcare to ask role-specific questions, write from an above-average understanding of healthcare, and produce high-quality career marketing documents.

Red Hat is at an exciting point in its journey. With a strong position across Enterprise Linux, automation, OpenShift, virtualization, AI and open source security, we are creating new conversations with customers and opening new markets.

Someone who is curious, commercially minded and proactive. Someone who creates momentum, brings people together and can engage confidently with everyone from technical experts to senior executives — without needing to be the loudest person in the room.


What you’ll do:

From day one, you’ll receive the training and support needed to leverage AI as a core tool for enhancing productivity, sparking creativity, and streamlining complex workflows.

Responsibilities

Primary Responsibilities

  • Interpret, organize, execute, and coordinate large substation engineering assignments with responsibility for budget, schedule, quality, and inter‑discipline coordination.
  • Plan and develop engineering projects involving unique or complex problems, offering specialized expertise in substation engineering.
  • Prepare substation layouts, one‑line and three‑line diagrams, schematics, and technical specifications.
  • Coordinate designs for steel structures, foundations, grounding grids, buswork, raceway, and conduit systems.
  • Specify and select substation equipment (e.g., transformers, breakers, switchgear, relays, instrument transformers).
  • Perform power system studies and analyses to support design decisions (load flow, short circuit, protection coordination, arc‑flash).
  • Provide design support during construction, respond to RFIs, and review/approve major items involving materials, equipment, and field construction.
  • Stamp/seal drawings and documents, including those for which you serve as the professional in responsible charge, per applicable jurisdictional statutes.
  • Plan, organize, supervise, and review the work of engineers and designers assigned to the project; participate in mentoring activities within the department.
  • Maintain liaison with internal and external stakeholders, acting independently on technical matters within the substation discipline.

Compliance & Safety

  • Ensure adherence to IEEE, ANSI, NEMA, NESC, and utility standards, as well as SSOE quality procedures.
  • Implement safety protocols for high‑voltage environments within design practices and during construction support.

Coordination

  • Collaborate with project managers, contractors, AHJs, and utility representatives to ensure design accuracy and constructability.
  • Review vendor drawings and perform QA/QC checks on design deliverables; coordinate multi‑discipline interfaces.

Innovation

  • Integrate SCADA systems, networking, and protective relaying into substation designs and upgrades.
  • Stay current with emerging technologies and sustainability practices applicable to substation engineering.

  • Competitive Salary: $130k – $170k / year depending on location, education, experience, and certifications.
  • Bonus and Incentives: Eligibility for our annual target bonus/incentive program based on company and individual performance and goals.
  • Ownership Opportunities: As an employee‑owned firm, we offer ownership opportunities to all employees at the associate level and above.
  • Comprehensive Benefits: Health, dental, and vision insurance, life insurance, 401(k) with company match, professional development and training, generous PTO, and paid holidays.

Additional Perks

  • Dynamic Culture: Supportive culture where you are an essential and highly valued member of our team.
  • Exciting Projects: Work on innovative projects from inception to completion with global, market‑leading clients.
  • Continuous Learning: A culture that celebrates curiosity, welcomes new ideas, and supports career growth.
  • Career Stability: Diverse market sectors, project types, and geographies help insulate your career from economic cycles.
  • Career Advancement: Structured career journey with abundant opportunities for growth and advancement.
  • Holistic Compensation: Benefits that support well‑being, work‑life balance, and financial success.

Qualifications

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering from an ABET‑accredited program; PE license preferred. EIT required if PE not yet obtained.
  • Twelve (12)+ years of related practical experience in substation design and engineering. Experience in lieu of professional license may be considered at SSOE’s discretion.
  • Demonstrated experience with substation physical layout design, including equipment arrangement, bus configurations, electrical clearances, grounding considerations, and overall yard layout for medium and high-voltage substations.
  • Proven experience with Protection & Control (P&C) systems, including protective relaying, control schematics, relay protection schemes, SCADA integration, and related substation design deliverables.
  • Demonstrated knowledge in: HV (>115 kV)/MV substation/switchgear design and substation yard layout; utility coordination; LV (480V/400V) plant power distribution interfaces; on‑site generation (stand‑by, prime, co‑gen, renewables) and UPS systems.
  • Proficiency with design and analysis tools such as AutoCAD, ETAP or similar power system analysis software, and protection relay settings/configuration.
  • Strong analytical, problem‑solving, communication, and teamwork skills; ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.
  • Experience supporting integrated transmission and substation projects from conceptual design through construction and commissioning strongly preferred.

Travel & Licensing

  • Travel required for site visits and commissioning activities.
  • Valid driver’s license required (may be waived for international assignments).
  • Maintains continuing professional education as required by registered states (voluntary or mandatory).

Senior Director, Logistics


Status: Exempt (Salaried)

Department: Logistics


Position Summary

The Senior Director of Logistics provides leadership for Plug Power’s hydrogen logistics transportation functions. This role is responsible for defining and executing a scalable, cost-effective, and compliant logistics strategy that supports enterprise growth and operational excellence. This North America role (excluding Europe operations) leads up to 5 direct reports and carries responsibility for total transportation and logistics spend of $15M+ annually.

The Senior Director role leads the logistics organization, ensuring efficient movement and delivery of hydrogen, a safety-critical cryogenic hazardous material handled in both bulk liquid (LH2) and gaseous form, to customers while driving continuous improvement, risk mitigation, and technology enablement. This leader partners closely with Executive Leadership and cross-functional teams to align logistics capabilities with business priorities, support complex projects, and enhance overall supply chain performance.


Core Duties and Responsibilities


  • Leads the strategy, planning, and execution for the movement and delivery of hydrogen and related products to customers and suppliers, ensuring safe, reliable, and cost-effective operations.
  • Owns the transportation function and partners closely with Supply Operations, Engineering, and the Fuel Product Manager to align transport execution with sourcing, production, and product strategy.
  • Establishes scalable logistics network strategies to support North America expansion, infrastructure development, and increasing operational complexity.
  • Leads logistics capacity and asset planning, including cryogenic trailer fleet sizing, terminal and fueling infrastructure, and the associated capital plan.
  • Provides oversight of all transportation modes, including bulk cryogenic liquid hydrogen and gaseous tube-trailer transport (the primary modes by cost and risk),
  • Ensures logistics readiness and execution for new product launches, hydrogen deployments, and large-scale energy and infrastructure projects.
  • Ensures adherence to compliance best practices and regulatory requirements while proactively mitigating risk.
  • Builds and leads a high-performing, North America logistics organization, including talent development, succession planning, and organizational design.
  • Drives enterprise-wide continuous improvement, cost optimization, and operational excellence across logistics operations, with explicit accountability for delivery costs and for product-loss (boil-off / venting) yield from load point to customer delivery.
  • Establishes and monitors executive-level KPIs and reporting, including delivery cost per kg, on-time-in-full (OTIF), trailer utilization and turns, boil-off / product-loss rate, carrier performance, and DOT-recordable safety incident rate, to ensure performance, accountability, and alignment with business objectives and is able and comfortable reporting out to Executive Leadership and/or Board of Directors regarding such KPIs.
  • Leads strategic sourcing and management of logistics providers, i.e. Logistics Sub-contractors
  • Partners cross-functionally with Executive Leadership, Product Management, Finance, Legal, Procurement, Engineering, and Operations to align logistics strategy with business priorities.
  • Ensures logistics performance meets the service obligations embedded in customer hydrogen supply agreements, including service levels, contingency and backup-supply commitments, and force-majeure provisions.
  • Oversees risk management and business continuity planning to ensure resilience across the North America hydrogen network.
  • Owns hazardous-materials emergency-response readiness, including spill/release response, incident command, carrier and driver training, and coordination with first responders and regulators following a transportation incident.
  • Evaluates and implements logistics technologies, systems, and digital solutions to enhance scalability, efficiency, and visibility.
  • Provides oversight of issue resolution, quality, and corrective actions across the supply chain.

•Travels as required.

•Performs all other duties as assigned.


Education and Experience


  • Master’s degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, or related field; equivalent experience considered.
  • 10+ years of logistics or supply chain experience, including leadership in complex, high-growth environments. Experience with cryogenics preferred.
  • Deep expertise in transportation and logistics strategy, preferably within energy, industrial, or infrastructure sectors.
  • Experience with hydrogen, hazardous materials, or over-dimensional logistics strongly preferred.
  • Proven track record of building and scaling organizations, driving transformation, and delivering operational excellence.
  • Strong financial acumen, including budgeting, cost optimization, and contract negotiation.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence executive stakeholders and lead cross-functional alignment.
  • Track record managing agreements across the full lifecycle - sourcing, negotiation, rate-adjustment windows, claims, and renewal.
  • Proven experience negotiating, structuring, and administering multi-year transportation and logistics agreements with individual annual contract values of $1M+, or aggregate/total contract value of $5M+, including complex commercial terms such as index- or fuel-surcharge-based pricing, take-or-pay and minimum-volume commitments, rate-adjustment mechanisms, and liability/indemnity provisions. Knowledge of the hazardous-materials and motor-carrier rules central to hydrogen transport (PHMSA / 49 CFR HMR, FMCSA Hours-of-Service, CDL hazmat and tanker endorsements, CGA standards), as well as broader DOT regulations, C-TPAT, and global trade compliance frameworks.
  • Experience implementing and maturing Transportation Management Systems, logistics technologies, and advanced operational methodologies.
  • Exceptional leadership, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Sound judgment operating in a safety-critical environment, including the ability to weigh reliability, safety, and cost trade-offs under time pressure.
  • High level of professionalism, integrity, and accountability.

About the Company

At OneClick Code, we are revolutionizing the roofing and restoration industry through smart automation, data transparency, and instant access to critical building information. Our mission is to empower contractors, adjusters, and insurance professionals with accurate, jurisdiction-specific codes and permit data, instantly, so they can work smarter, not harder.

Founded in 2018, with a vision to eliminate the inefficiencies and guesswork that slow down claims and repairs, OneClick Code has become the go-to platform for accessing trusted roofing codes, manufacturer specifications, tax jurisdiction data, and permit requirements, all in just one click.

We're a fast-growing, venture-backed startup that thrives on innovation, collaboration, and impact. As we scale, we're looking for mission-driven team members who are passionate about using technology to bring clarity and confidence to an often-overlooked corner of the construction world.

The Opportunity

The Senior Data & Analytics Engineer will own the reliability and evolution of the company’s data and analytics infrastructure, including data models, the warehouse, pipelines, integrations, and billing data. This role moves beyond reporting into data modeling, analytics architecture, instrumentation strategy, and cross-functional enablement. The person will independently identify opportunities, translate ambiguous business needs into clear analytics initiatives, and drive those initiatives from definition through implementation and adoption.

This individual will serve as the technical bridge between raw data and business decision-making, leading the design of robust data models, optimizing SaaS metrics, and ensuring accurate tracking across web and native applications. Success in this role requires ownership of both technical quality and business outcomes.

This is a senior individual-contributor role. The person is expected to demonstrate leadership through initiative ownership, sound judgment, proactive communication, and cross-functional influence. People management is not currently a requirement.

Responsibilities

Analytics Architecture & Data Modeling

  • Design, build, and maintain scalable analytics data models to support business reporting and decision-making.
  • Build, maintain, and troubleshoot ETL/ELT pipelines and data transformations.
  • Own source-of-truth definitions and reconcile data across application, billing, and analytics systems.
  • Own the structure and optimization of SaaS metrics, including subscription lifecycle, billing, churn, retention, LTV, and revenue analytics (Stripe).
  • Ensure data integrity, consistency, and governance across systems.
  • Monitor data flows and proactively detect, troubleshoot, and recover from pipeline failures or missing data.
  • Partner with Engineering to assess the data impact of product releases and prevent breaking changes to collection systems.

Instrumentation & Event Tracking

  • Define tracking specifications and lead the auditing and validation of event strategy across web and native applications in partnership with Engineering.
  • Partner with engineering and product teams to define, implement, and audit tracking standards.
  • Improve reliability and completeness of user event data (Segment, Mixpanel, or similar tools).

Data Analysis & Insights

  • Perform advanced analysis using SQL and Python to generate actionable insights.
  • Identify trends, risks, and growth opportunities within SaaS performance metrics.
  • Translate complex datasets into clear business recommendations for leadership.

Analytics Platform Ownership

  • Build and continuously improve the company’s analytics framework and reporting ecosystem.
  • Develop dashboards and data visualization assets that provide reliable, self-serve insights for stakeholders.
  • Optimize data pipelines and queries for performance and scalability.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Lead cross-functional analytics initiatives by aligning Product, Engineering, Customer Success, and Finance on the business problem, requirements, KPIs, measurement approach, milestones, and expected outcomes.
  • Act as the subject-matter expert in analytics and data interpretation across the organization.
  • Proactively surface relevant trends, risks, and opportunities, and provide leadership with clear recommendations and forecasting support.

Initiative Leadership & Ownership

  • Independently identify and prioritize analytics opportunities aligned with business needs.
  • Lead analytics initiatives from problem definition and stakeholder alignment through implementation, adoption, and measurement of results.
  • Establish clear scope, milestones, success criteria, and ownership for assigned initiatives.
  • Proactively communicate progress, risks, tradeoffs, and decisions needed to the manager and relevant stakeholders.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in analytics engineering, analytics, or related data-focused roles, preferably in a SaaS environment, including demonstrated ownership of complex cross-functional initiatives.
  • Strong proficiency in SQL (advanced querying, modeling, performance optimization).
  • Experience using Python for data analysis and automation.

jobs.description:
Overview: Securing the CI/CD Pipeline

The DevSecOps Engineer is responsible for automating, integrating, and enforcing security controls throughout the entire development lifecycle, from code commit to production deployment. You will be the vital link between Development, Security, and Operations, ensuring that the continuous integration and delivery pipelines for our e-commerce platform, internal tools, and AI agents are secure by design.

Internship Details

Duration: 3 months

Start Date: Immediate

Location: Remote

Stipend: None initially. Based on your first-quarter performance, you may be offered a paid full-time opportunity, or even be absorbed directly by the client as an FTE.

Key Responsibilities & Core Projects

You will embed security into the automation processes across the entire tech stack.

  • Security Automation (CI/CD): Integrate automated security scanning tools, including Static Application Security Testing (SAST) and Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), directly into our CI/CD pipelines (managed via Makefile and automated testing pipelines).

  • Infrastructure Security: Enforce secure Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) practices using Terraform for provisioning and managing our Oracle Cloud Free VMs. Continuously monitor the cloud infrastructure for vulnerabilities and misconfigurations.

  • Container and Runtime Security: Manage and secure the application deployment environment by implementing robust container security policies for Docker and ensuring runtime threat detection and logging for production services.

  • Collaboration & Remediation: Collaborate directly with development teams to promote secure coding practices, provide guidance on vulnerability remediation, and ensure security findings are addressed before deployment.

  • Secrets Management: Implement automated injection and rotation of secrets using Vault into the applications and deployment environment.

  • Observability Integration: Integrate security logs and metrics into the observability stack (Prometheus, Grafana, Loki) to ensure real-time security monitoring and alerting.

Required Technologies & Tools

Candidates must have strong hands-on experience in both DevOps automation and security implementation:

  • Automation/CI/CD: Makefile, automated testing, scripting (Bash/Python/Node.js).

  • Security Tools: SAST/DAST tools, vulnerability scanners, runtime protection.

  • Infrastructure: Terraform (IaC), Docker, Oracle Cloud/equivalent IaaS.

  • Security & Auth: Vault (Secrets Management), Traefik (Edge Security), Observability stack (Prometheus, Loki).

  • Codebase: Experience securing applications built with Node.js/NestJS and Next.js/React/TypeScript.

AI Agent Focus

You will ensure the secure deployment and operation of our AI layer.

  • Secure Deployment: Implement dedicated, hardened deployment pipelines for AI agents (built on LangChain/LlamaIndex), isolating them and controlling their access to core supply chain data (MES, WMS, OMS).

  • Runtime Monitoring: Establish specific security logging and monitoring for LLM-related services to detect unusual access patterns or potential data leakage.

Success Metrics & Career Path

Performance will be measured by:

  • Pipeline Security: Percentage of security checks automated and integrated into the CI/CD pipeline.

  • Vulnerability Reduction: Measurable reduction in critical and high-priority findings in production and pre-production environments.

  • Compliance: Successful auditing and enforcement of secure IaC and container security policies.

Mentorship Structure: Reports to the Solution Architect or DevOps Lead, working directly with infrastructure and development teams to implement security-as-code.

jobs.description:
Localpaymentis a fintech company specializing in local and cross-border payment solutions for emerging markets. Our platform enables global companies to accept payments in local currencies through native methods in each country, facilitating their international expansion.

In 2024, Localpayment entered into a strategic partnership withAleph Group, a global technology and digital media company. This collaboration enhances our capabilities and reach, combining robust payment infrastructure with a broader digital ecosystem.

We are looking for aRegulatory Specialistto join our Compliance & Legal team and help us navigate the complex payments regulatory landscape across Latin America. You'll own the lifecycle of payment licenses across the region, monitor regulatory changes, and ensure Localpayment operates in full compliance as we expand into new markets. If you know what it really takes to obtain, maintain, and monitor payment licenses across LATAM — we want to hear from you.

Responsibilities

  • Own the full lifecycle of payment licenses across LATAM markets — from initial filing to renewals and regulatory amendments

  • Monitor and analyze regulatory changes from central banks and financial supervisory authorities (BACEN, CNBV, BCRA, SFC, CMF, SBS, and others), and translate them into actionable internal guidance

  • Build and maintain direct relationships with regulators — coordinate responses to inquiries and represent Localpayment in regulatory interactions

  • Support the design and implementation of AML/KYC programs aligned with local regulations in each country where we operate

  • Lead regulatory analysis for expansion into new markets, including license mapping, risk assessment, and timelines

  • Collaborate with Product, Tech, and Ops teams to ensure regulatory compliance is embedded in how we build and operate — not bolted on after the fact

  • Maintain and update internal compliance policies, procedures, and manuals to reflect evolving regulatory landscapes across the region

  • Use AI tools (Claude, NotebookLM, or equivalent) to accelerate regulatory research, policy drafting, and compliance documentation.

Requirements

  • 3–5 years of experience in Regulatory Affairs, Compliance, or Legal roles within fintechs or payments companies.

  • Direct, hands-on experience with payment or e-money licenses in at least 2 LATAM markets. Experience with cross-border payments, PSP ecosystems, or acquiring bank relationships is a great plus.

  • Working knowledge of AML/KYC/PLD requirements across the region.

  • Familiarity with key regulators: BACEN, CNBV, BCRA, SFC, CMF, SBS/BCRP.

  • Law, accounting, or related degree with a regulatory or financial focus.

  • Fluent Spanish (required) · Intermediate-advanced English (required). Portuguese (a strong plus for Brazil market coverage)

  • Ability to translate complex regulatory language into clear, actionable business guidance.

  • Autonomous and proactive — you spot regulatory risks before they become operational problems

Benefits

  • Real regulatory complexity, real scope.You'll manage licenses across 17 active markets, with expansion ongoing. This isn't a single-country compliance role — it's a regional portfolio with meaningful stakes.

  • Backed by Aleph Group's global network. Operating in 130+ markets, Aleph gives Localpayment access, credibility, and resources that most fintechs our size don't have. That matters when you're negotiating with regulators.

  • Your work shapes how we expand. Every new market Localpayment enters starts with the regulatory groundwork you lay. You're not supporting the business — you're enabling it.

  • Competitive compensation + growth opportunities. USD-denominated salary, performance bonus, learning budget, and direct access to senior leadership from day one.

About Ridgeline

Ridgeline is the first front-to-back system of record for investment managers. Founded by visionary entrepreneur Dave Duffield (co-founder of both PeopleSoft and Workday), the company was created to modernize an industry held back by outdated, disconnected technology. Powered by a single, real-time data set and embedded AI, Ridgeline helps firms automate complexity, accelerate collaboration, and deliver tailored client experiences at scale, without added headcount or risk. Ridgeline is headquartered in Lake Tahoe, with offices in New York, Reno, and the Bay Area, and is recognized by Fast Company as a “Best Workplace for Innovators,” by Frost & Sullivan as a “Technology Innovation Leader,” and by The Software Report as a “Top 100 Software Company.”

Why this role exists

Ridgeline is growing into relationships with some of the largest and most complex organizations in investment management. As a Strategic Sales Executive, you will open and lead these relationships at the most senior levels of the client organization, working alongside solutions consultants, partners, and leaders across Ridgeline. It is a new and visible motion for the company, with real opportunity to shape how we approach it.

What success looks like

Within your first year, you will have established credible relationships with senior stakeholders at your priority accounts, built a clear multi-year plan for each, and created real momentum toward a contract decision. You will be known as a trusted partner by clients and colleagues alike.

What you'll do

  • Identify, pursue, and open new strategic accounts at large financial institutions through prospecting and strategic planning.
  • Build trusted relationships with senior executives and a broad range of stakeholders across the client organization, adapting your style to each.
  • Lead executive conversations around business outcomes such as growing revenue, lowering cost, and launching new products.
  • Develop and execute multi-year strategic account plans that carry an opportunity through strategy, evaluation, and implementation planning.
  • Orchestrate internal and external resources, including solutions consultants, partners, and executive sponsors, to move complex opportunities forward.
  • Navigate formal procurement and approval processes with patience and precision, delivering a high-touch experience at every interaction.
  • Travel extensively to meet clients and partners wherever the influence sits.

What we look for

  • 10+ years of direct experience selling complex software into large, process-driven organizations such as large financial institutions, government, or higher education.
  • A track record as a hunter: you’ve personally opened and won large accounts rather than managing or expanding existing relationships.
  • Experience closing large, multi-year deals with many stakeholders and formal evaluation processes.
  • Exceptional emotional intelligence and humility: you build trust quickly, learn fast, are comfortable saying “I don’t know,” and bring in the right people to help.
  • The range to connect with very different stakeholders, from senior executives to operational teams.
  • Meticulous attention to detail and a high-touch approach to every client interaction.
  • Willingness and ability to travel extensively.
  • Strong drive and genuine enthusiasm for Ridgeline and for building something new.

Compensation & Benefits

The cash compensation amount for this role is targeted at $400,000 - $460,000 OTE. Final compensation amounts are determined by multiple factors, including candidate experience and expertise, and may vary from the amount listed above.

July 2026

TITLE:Manager, Grant Operations & Admin - Workforce Innovation & SystemsRESPONSIBLE TO:Senior Director, Grant Operations & AdministrationDIVISION/DEPT:Mission Services, Grant Operations & AdministrationSUPERVISES:No direct reports expected; provides dotted line portfolio direction to Specialist(s)FLSA STATUS:Exempt

SUMMARY

Manages the administrative backbone for the Workforce Innovation & Systems portfolio, including GDCA Digital Skills/LERs and Opportunity Accelerator grants.This position owns portfolio-level award activation, RFP/site-selection administration, sub-award lifecycle management, procurement/PO coordination, financial monitoring coordination, documentation integrity, and closeout discipline for high-volume private grants and sub-recipient activity.

NOTE:This position is supported by grants. The position’s establishment and continuance may be dependent upon on-going grant funding.

BASICFUNCTION:

  • Portfolio Management & Grant Lifecyle Oversight-Manage the Workforce Innovation & Systems grant administration portfolio across the full grant lifecycle (award through closeout), ensuring coordination, execution, and performance across multiple concurrent and private and public grants.
  • Compliance, Systems, and Operational Infrastructure- Establish and maintain standardized grant administration systems, tools, and processes (policies, SOPs, templates, trackers, and audit-readiness protocols) to ensure compliance with funder and enterprise requirements.
  • Cross-Functional Coordination & Risk Management
    Serve as the central coordination point across Program, Finance, Legal, and Development to operationalize grants, monitor financial and compliance performance, and proactively escalate risks to leadership.

SPECIFICDUTIES:

Portfolio Administration & Award Setup

  • Manage a portfolio of active grants, including federal and private funding streams.
  • Receive and log grant awards: review terms, conditions, reporting requirements, and operational implications in partnership with cross-functional stakeholders
  • Coordinate grant launch activities, including SharePoint setup, grant coding requests, financial tracking inputs and system access needs.

Systems, SOPs, & Documentation Management

  • Maintain portfolio-specific grant administration infrastructure, including policies, SOPs, templated, reporting trackers, compliance checklists, grant calendars, and audit-readiness tools.
  • Ensure alignment of all portfolio documentation with organization standards and evolving compliance expectations.

Request For Proposal (RFP) Administration

  • Lead administration setup and coordination of RFP and site selection process.
  • Sub-Award Lifecycle Management
  • Manage the full-sub award process including template preparation, documentation assembly, contract system submission and contract workflow coordination, site- specific subawards, budgets and attachments, signature tracking and execution.

Financial Coordination & Invoicing

  • Coordinate sub-award invoicing, procurement, and PO workflows in partnership with Finance and Program teams. Monitor portfolio financial activity and ensure adherence to federal and funder requirements.
  • Support the flow-down of compliance requirements to internal teams and sub-recipients.

Monitoring, Reporting and Compliance

  • Support ongoing grant monitoring activities including budget and financial reviews, subrecipient financial and documentation compliance checks, manage narrative report compilation in preparation for submission, set and manage site visits (virtual or on-site) monitoring schedules, performance reviews and corrective action plan tracking and resolution

Closeout & Audit Readiness

  • Lead grant closeout planning and execution, including final deliverables, documentation completeness, and archival processes.
  • Ensure audit readiness and compliance with funder closeout requirements.

Risk Escalation & Team Coordination

  • Identify and escalate compliance, financial, capacity or reporting risks to the Sr. Director
  • Coordinate with Specialist staff to ensure continuity, cross-training, and workload coverage across the portfolio

RELATIONSHIPS:

Internal:DailycontactwithGII team members to coordinate projects and support activities.

Local Goodwills:Frequent contact withrepresentativesofGoodwill member organizations.

External:Contactwithdonors, funders, vendors and partners.

SKILLSNEEDED:

  • Demonstrates the ability to consistently execute work with accuracy, timeliness, and accountability.
  • Maintain a strong understanding of regulatory, funder, and organizational requirements while proactively managing risk.
  • Builds productive working relationships and aligns stakeholders around common goals.
  • Communicates information clearly and maintains accurate, organized records to support accountability and transparency.
  • Demonstrates comprehensive understanding of the full grant management process from opportunity identification through closeout.
  • Seeks opportunities to improve efficiency, effectiveness, and scalability through process and systems enhancements.

EDUCATION:

Bachelor’s degree in Business or Public Administration, Nonprofit Management, Project Management, Human Services or a related field. Master’s degree preferred but not required. Professional certifications such as PMP, or grant management desirable.

EXPERIENCE:

Minimum 3-5 years of progressively responsible experience in grant administration,project management, nonprofit administration or other operational roles. Experience using Microsoft Office Suite, SharePoint, Excel-based tracking tools, dashboards and collaboration platforms.

DECISIONMAKING:

This position should exercise moderate independent judgment within established policies, procedures, and grant requirements.

SUPERVISION:

Works under general supervision with considerable latitude in organizing and executing assigned responsibilities. Work is reviewed for overall effectiveness, compliance, and results.

PHYSICALEFFORT:

Sedentarywithlifting10poundsmaximumandoccasionallylifting and/or carrying such articles or files. Walking and standing are required occasionally; long hours sitting at a desk and using a computer.

Our Values

We believe everyone deserves an opportunity to thrive. Goodwill’s mission grounds us and happens through each one of us. This aspiration applies to each GII team member as much as to the people we serve.

GII’s organizational values guide all that we do; how we do our work and make decisions, and how we interact with each other, Goodwill members and all stakeholders.

SKEELO: EMBARQUE NA JORNADA QUE COLOCA A LEITURA NO CENTRO DE TUDO. 🐿️

QUEM SOMOS 💚

O Skeelo é uma plataforma digital de leitura que conecta pessoas a e-books, audiobooks e minibooks em uma experiência acessível e personalizada. Desde 2019, usamos a tecnologia como um meio para democratizar o acesso à leitura e ampliar seu impacto no desenvolvimento das pessoas.

Acreditamos que ler vai além do lazer: é uma ferramenta poderosa para expandir repertórios, fortalecer o pensamento crítico e impulsionar o desenvolvimento humano.

NOSSA VIBE 💚

Estamos distribuídos e distribuídas pelo Brasil e pelo mundo, movidos por inovação, agilidade e aprendizado contínuo, que valoriza a diversidade e transforma a leitura para se adaptar à vida das pessoas. Fazemos tudo isso com transparência nas relações, coragem para inovar, foco em alta performance, olhar constante para encantar clientes e leitores e entregas ágeis que fazem a diferença.

Nosso modelo de trabalho é remote first, tirando o melhor do home office: autorresponsabilidade com autonomia. Porém também acreditamos na conexão e trocas dos encontros presenciais, desse modo, temos alguns encontros presenciais em São Paulo - SP, para conexão com os demais Skeelers. Mas relaxa, o Skeelo sempre organiza tudo pra gente.

O time de Conteúdo está precisando de alguém, e queremos você com a gente!

Sua missão? Atuar na frente de estratégia e curadoria de conteúdo do Skeelo, olhando para o mercado e para o catálogo de forma propositiva. Aqui você vai identificar tendências, encontrar oportunidades e lacunas no acervo em diferentes mercados e transformar isso em estratégias de conteúdo que conectem o engajamento dos leitores às necessidades do negócio.

O seu dia a dia no Skeelo vai ser assim:

  • Mapear tendências de consumo de leitura e de formatos nos mercados onde o Skeelo atua, com um olhar global;
  • Monitorar ativamente a cultura pop, as redes sociais e os mercados de entretenimento e livros para identificar temas em alta;
  • Analisar o catálogo de forma crítica, identificando gaps e oportunidades de fortalecimento em cada mercado;
  • Definir temas e conceitos de curadoria, como galerias, banners e palavras-chave, para otimizar a descoberta de títulos;
  • Realizar benchmarks constantes e atuar de forma orientada por dados, traduzindo análises em insights estratégicos com sensibilidade cultural;
  • Atuar em parceria com marketing, produto, dados e parcerias editoriais, alimentando os times com informações estratégicas sobre mercado e novos títulos.

Para isso, você vai precisar ter:

  • Experiência sólida no mercado de conteúdo, seja editorial, audiovisual ou outros segmentos;
  • Repertório cultural e criatividade para propor curadorias e estratégias de conteúdo;
  • Capacidade de entender modelos de negócio complexos e equilibrar estratégia de conteúdo com as necessidades da empresa;
  • Facilidade para lidar com múltiplas demandas e prioridades ao mesmo tempo;
  • Boa comunicação e facilidade para interagir com diferentes áreas;
  • Inglês fluente, com boa compreensão de leitura e escuta para avaliar conteúdos internacionais;
  • Espanhol intermediário, com foco em compreensão de textos e áudio.

E seria muito bom se você também tivesse:

  • Olhar editorial, com experiência em edição ou curadoria de livros;
  • Experiência com conteúdos de diferentes mercados internacionais;
  • Familiaridade com Excel e ferramentas de IA no dia a dia de trabalho.

E os benefícios? A gente cuida bem de quem constrói isso aqui 💚

  • Plano de saúde (sem custo e sem coparticipação para você e seus familiares) + odonto e seguro de vida
  • VA/VR flexível no Caju (liberdade real de uso)
  • Bem-estar completo: Totalpass (atividade física) + ZenKlub (saúde mental)
  • PPR anual atrelado a metas e impacto
  • Acesso ao Skeelo Premium + clube do livro com ebook do mês
  • Auxílio creche + licença parental estendida
  • Parceria com escolas de idiomas, Berlitz e Open English
  • Feriados de SP emendados + recesso remunerado no fim do ano
  • Day off de aniversário

Quer ver tudo com mais detalhes? Dá uma olhada na nossa página de carreiras:

DEU MATCH? ENTÃO VEM CÁ! 💚

Se você busca desenvolvimento e quer gerar impacto facilitando o acesso à leitura, vem construir sua carreira com a gente. Esse papel principal pode ser seu, está esperando o que para se inscrever? #ValeAPenaSerSkeeler

jobs.description:
Academic Communities Intern

At a glance: Fully remote · Must live in AL, CO, DC, FL, GA, IL, IN, LA, MA, MI, MN, NC, NJ, NY, OH, OR, PA, TN, TX, VA, WA, or WI · Pay: $18.00 per hour · Maximum hours per week: 24 · Dates of Internship: January 19th, 2027 - April 9th, 2027

The impact of this role

You will support the academic community of marketers within the American Marketing Association by providing exciting and unique opportunities for members to engage with the profession. This role will provide administrative support for the Academic Communities team by delivering community-driven events, supporting volunteer leaders, and continuing to foster a “sense of home” for fellowship and camaraderie among academics.

What you'll do

  • Maintain and manage Special Interest Group (SIG) webpages.
  • Assist with SIG budget and financial management, including payments, reimbursements, and invoices.
  • Support the Manager, Academic Communities, with planning and logistics for the 2027 Winter Academic, Virtual Winter Academic, Summer Academic, and Marketing and Public Policy conferences.
  • Respond to attendee inquiries alongside the Manager, Academic Communities, and Customer Support team.
  • Help execute Conference and SIG awards processes.
  • Assist the Senior Copy Editor with conference proceedings administration.

What you bring

  • High school diploma
  • Enrolled at a 2-year or 4-year college/university
  • Customer service or volunteer management experience
  • Interest in working within event management, volunteer management, or association management
  • Experience in Google Suite
  • Keen eye for detail
  • Ability to work remotely 24 hours per week

What you may also have

  • Experience planning events at any scale preferred

Why the AMA

The AMA is the essential community for marketers, from students to executives to academics. Through our five scholarly journals, conferences, PCM® certification, 70 regional chapters, and presence on 350 college campuses, we help the profession learn, grow, and make a lasting impact. The AMA Foundation (AMAF) strengthens and elevates the marketing profession by advancing knowledge, building a global community of marketing leaders, and supporting marketing initiatives that drive innovation and societal impact. Want to learn more about AMA? Check out our website.

What it's like here

  • Fridays are ours. No internal meetings after 12 pm. Use that time to catch up, explore learning and development, or whatever you need to avoid the Sunday Scaries!
  • Remote, but not alone. Teammates in 20+ states, annual team member summit in Chicago, monthly town halls, and lots of cross-team collaboration.
  • Recognition is built in.Our Bucketlist rewards program enables gratitude in tangible form!
  • Growth: Free AMA membership, professional development content, and the PCM® Marketing Manager certification exam
  • Flexibility: We know you may have a balance of classes and this internship. We offer flexibility with your schedule.

How we hire

  1. Resume review by our recruiter and the hiring manager. A person reads your resume; AMA never uses AI to screen candidates.
  2. One-way video interview (Spark Hire): Five (5) questions, about 15-20 minutes, unlimited think time. We promise it isn't scary. We wrote the questions carefully because we want your answers to be just as thoughtful. Our recruiter is the face you’ll see asking the questions. No robots here.
  3. 30-minute phone interview with a member of the People and Culture team.
  4. Virtual interview with the hiring manager.

We won’t leave you hanging. You will always hear from us within a week about the status of your application and status.

Please note that only applicants who apply officially will be considered in this process. We appreciate the candidates who apply and express interest, but we cannot circumvent the recruitment process for any candidates, regardless of their relationship to the AMA or our team members.

Eligibility

You must live in one of the states listed above. Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without employer sponsorship. For internships, F-1 visas are okay.

Equal opportunity

The American Marketing Association is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, reproductive health decisions, family responsibilities, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with applicable legal requirements. AMA is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

jobs.description:
Overview

DecisionPoint seeks a Journeyman Endpoint Security / ESS Engineer to support endpoint-security administration, policy enforcement, agent health, compliance reporting, and security-event investigation for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program.

The Endpoint Security / ESS Engineer will serve as a McAfee endpoint-security specialist supporting the Department of Defense Endpoint Security Solutions environment. The engineer will investigate security events, unhealthy agents, policy failures, and endpoint-compliance issues; implement approved corrective actions; and validate that required endpoint protections remain operational and effective.

This role will coordinate agent deployment and endpoint remediation activities with Task 4 infrastructure personnel, support cybersecurity incident reporting, and maintain technical evidence for security-control and authorization activities.

This position is remote, with a preference for candidates located in the Chicago area.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

The Endpoint Security / ESS Engineer will:

  • Serve as a technical specialist for the McAfee/Trellix endpoint-security technologies supporting the DoD Endpoint Security Solutions environment.
  • Support administration, configuration, maintenance, and monitoring of approved endpoint-security tools and services.
  • Implement and maintain approved endpoint-security policies, configurations, exclusions, rules, and enforcement settings.
  • Monitor endpoint agents for connectivity, communication, deployment, update, and operational-health issues.
  • Investigate unhealthy, inactive, noncommunicating, outdated, or improperly configured endpoint agents.
  • Diagnose policy-enforcement failures, update failures, deployment errors, and endpoint-protection gaps.
  • Implement Government-approved corrective actions and validate that endpoint protections have been successfully restored.
  • Review ESS reports and dashboards to identify security events, compliance issues, policy failures, and remediation needs.
  • Investigate endpoint-security alerts and events and coordinate response activities with cybersecurity, infrastructure, application, and Government teams.
  • Coordinate McAfee/Trellix agent deployment, upgrade, repair, removal, and replacement activities with Task 4 infrastructure personnel.
  • Support endpoint-remediation activities involving operating-system configurations, security policies, agents, signatures, content updates, and approved software.
  • Confirm that endpoints receive required policies, signatures, content, and product updates.
  • Validate endpoint compliance following remediation, configuration changes, maintenance, or agent deployment.
  • Track endpoint-security findings, assigned owners, corrective actions, dependencies, deadlines, and closure evidence.
  • Support vulnerability remediation associated with endpoint-security configurations, agent health, or protection status.
  • Collect and maintain logs, screenshots, reports, configuration information, and other evidence supporting remediation and compliance.
  • Create and update incident, problem, change, and remediation tickets in the designated workflow platform.
  • Support cybersecurity incident reporting by gathering relevant endpoint data, event details, logs, timelines, and investigative evidence.
  • Escalate significant events, persistent policy failures, widespread agent-health issues, and unresolved compliance deficiencies.
  • Coordinate with system administrators and asset-management personnel to reconcile endpoint records, agent status, and authoritative inventories.
  • Support security-control testing and provide endpoint-security evidence for RMF, ATO, ATC, audit, and inspection activities.
  • Develop endpoint-security compliance reports, agent-health summaries, event metrics, trend analyses, and briefing materials.
  • Maintain endpoint-security procedures, configuration documentation, standard operating procedures, troubleshooting guides, and technical knowledge articles.
  • Recommend technical and process improvements that strengthen endpoint protection, agent health, monitoring, and compliance reporting.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Active Secret clearance or higher.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 7 years of relevant cybersecurity, endpoint-security, information-assurance, or information-security experience.
  • Current CompTIA Security+ certification.
  • Hands-on experience administering or supporting McAfee endpoint-security technologies.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting DoD Endpoint Security Solutions in an enterprise environment.
  • Experience with McAfee or Trellix ePolicy Orchestrator, Endpoint Security, McAfee Agent, threat-prevention modules, firewall policies, and web-control capabilities.
  • Experience monitoring and remediating unhealthy, inactive, noncommunicating, or noncompliant endpoint agents.
  • Experience troubleshooting agent deployment, policy enforcement, signature updates, content distribution, and endpoint-protection failures.
  • Experience analyzing endpoint-security events, alerts, logs, dashboards, and compliance reports.
  • Experience coordinating endpoint remediation with infrastructure, desktop-support, network, application, and cybersecurity teams.
  • Familiarity with Host Based Security System technologies or legacy McAfee capabilities used within DoD environments.
  • Experience supporting cybersecurity incident analysis, evidence collection, escalation, and reporting.
  • Knowledge of the DoD Risk Management Framework, NIST SP 800-53 controls, DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides, and applicable DoD endpoint-security requirements.
  • Experience providing technical evidence for ATO, ATC, security-control assessment, audit, or inspection activities.
  • Familiarity with ACAS or Tenable, STIG Viewer, SCAP tools, eMASS, ServiceNow, or comparable cybersecurity and workflow platforms.
  • Experience reconciling endpoint-agent status with configuration-management or asset-inventory records.
  • Experience developing endpoint-compliance reports, agent-health metrics, event trends, and remediation dashboards.
  • Additional certifications such as CySA+, CASP+, CISSP, Trellix product certifications, or equivalent cybersecurity credentials.
  • Familiarity with current DoD 8140 cybersecurity workforce qualification requirements.
  • Strong troubleshooting, analytical, documentation, communication, and cross-functional coordination skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple endpoint-security events, remediation activities, and technical dependencies in a structured enterprise environment.

Our Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

It is the policy of DecisionPoint Corporation to provide equal employment opportunity in accordance with all applicable Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action laws, directives and regulations to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other protected status under Federal, State or Local laws.

However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor's legal duty to furnish information.
